Also, you will be able to show your abilities in the Story Mode, Versus Mode, Group Battle Mode, Tournament Mode, or the very Mr. Satan Mode, in which you play as Mr. Satan betting on who will win each match.
Dragon Force

The world of Legendra was ruled by benevolent goddesses, but the last of them, Astea, was challenged by a dark god named Madruk. In order to defeat Madruk, Astea created a powerful dragon, who eventually emerged victorious and was able to seal Madruk away.

Years have passed. Legendra is now divided into eight kingdoms. One of them, Fandaria, is ruled by a monarch named Goldark. The other kings have heard rumors that Goldark is planning to take over Legendra by conquering all the other kingdoms. Everyone is preparing for the war, without realizing that the ancient evil is about to raise its head once again...

Dragon Force is a real-time strategy game (RTS). The player can choose one of the six monarchs (plus two additional ones that become available once the game is completed) with their unique scenarios. The gameplay is divided into three modes: management, overworld movement, and battle.
Dragon Force II: Kamisarishi Daichi ni

Dragon Force II: Kamisarishi Daichi ni is a real-time strategy and role-playing and the follow-up to Dragon Force. It is set 500 years after the events of the first game. The player follows a group of monarchs that come together to face a new threat looming over Legendra. The story also delves into what happened to the original Dragon Force after Madruk's defeat.

Compared to the first game it adds a laboratory system which lets the player research new skills. It also introduces the capacity to have two separate types of soldiers in the same army, thus allowing ground troops to be aided by air troops, for instance.
Dragon Master Silk

The plot of this semi-comical RPG is rather simple: an angelic creature named Silk must defeat the Prince of Darkness, who rules his own dungeon full of claustrophobic corridors and monsters. Aided by her lovely companions Ao, Aka, and Ki (which means blue, red, and yellow in Japanese), Silk must deal with the evil Prince and his minions.

Dragon Master Silk is a dungeon crawler with Japanese-style turn-based combat. The entire game is viewed from first person perspective. The largest bulk of the game is navigating 3D dungeons, fighting regular enemies and bosses. The game maintains a distinct comical style, evident in graphics and character design.
Dragon's Dream

Dragon's Dream is an online multiplayer dungeon-crawler RPG which operated from December 1997 through September 1999. Comparable to classic Wizardry games, players form a party of up to four adventurers, then enter a tile-based dungeon searching for loot, fighting monsters in a turn-based format, and ultimately attempting to complete various quests. During crawls, each player controls one character in the party and can communicate with each other via text chat. There are five different classes and eight playable races to choose from.

Outside the dungeon, numerous locations are available in the town which provide specific functions; for example, the tavern lets players chat and form parties, the guild lets players create characters and accept mission requests, and the post office lets players send messages directly between one another.
DragonHeart: Fire & Steel

Dragonheart: Fire and Steel was released to the public in 1996, and is a 2D side scrolling beat 'em up based off of the movie of the same name. Players take on the role of a retired knight who must return to action and remain true to the oaths he took long ago. An evil prince's tyranny threatens the land, and the knight (who was a former dragonslayer) can only defeat this scheming noble with the help of a friend who just happens to be the last surviving dragon on Earth.

DragonHeart puts you in the sweaty medieval shoes of dragon hunter Bowen, as he faces the last dragons still surviving, and then ends up befriending one, Draco. With his help, he goes after King Einon, a former pupil of the dragon hunter, who has turned to evil.

Dragonheart's gameplay is quite similar to the Golden Axe series.
Dream Generation: Koi ka? Shigoto ka!?...

Dream Generation: Koi ka? Shigoto ka!?... is a raising simulation & love adventure game. The player controls 19-year-old Toranosuke Rokujō, an aimless college student who has no idea what he wants out of life. After meeting up with a group of his high-school classmates, he decides it's time to get his life in order, find a job, and find a girlfriend within the next year.

The simulation gameplay generally consists of deciding Toranosuke's schedule for each weekday: when and for how long to go to work, study, exercise, and rest. He will need to work to earn money for food and rent, study to improve his job prospects, and exercise to keep his health and energy up. During free time and on Saturdays and holidays, he can explore the town on foot to visit various locations, go shopping and meet the other characters.
Dream Square: Hinagata Akiko

Dream Square is a multimedia fan disc featuring singer and actress Akiko Hinagata. It includes photo and video galleries of the idol and her music, interview clips, and various other bits of information, all presented as the player getting a personal tour of her house. There is also a puzzle mode where the player must unscramble photographs within a time limit. The package also includes a 1997–2001 calendar.
Druid: Yami e no Tsuisekisha

The world of Navan has many islands, and four of them are reigned by the powerful Druid brothers: Lawson, Curak, Havnar, and Astor. They worship different deities and try to maintain the harmony of nature on their islands. But one day, Lawson mysteriously disappears. Unable to solve the mystery, the brothers seek out you, a grandson of a once powerful Druid, to search for Lawson in the entire world of Navan.

The gameplay of Druid is somewhat similar to that of Ultima VIII: Pagan. It is an action RPG with simple point-and-click interface and action-oriented combat. You can execute two different types of physical attacks (high and low) and cast a variety of spells. You don't have a party in the game.
Duke Nukem 3D

Aliens have landed in futuristic Los Angeles and it's up to the Duke to bring the pain and show them the door. After the initial entries of side-scrolling platform games, Duke Nukem 3D introduces a first-person perspective to the series and turns the game into a full-fledged shooter with 2.5D graphics.

Duke's arsenal includes pistols, pipe bombs, laser trip mines, Nordenfelt guns, a chain gun and various rocket launchers, but also his mighty foot to kick enemies. The game sports a high level of interactivity. Many objects in the environment can be broken or interacted with, such as pool tables, arcade machines, glass, light switches and security cameras. The protagonist is also able to hand strippers dollars to have them remove their top.

The main character regularly delivers commentary on the events through one-liners.
Dungeon Master Nexus

Dungeon Master Nexus is the first game in the Dungeon Master series using a 3D graphics engine. The game features 3 dungeons with 15 levels in total. Upon entering the ground level of the dungeon, the player is to compose his party made up of up to 4 heroes from the "Hall of Champions". Throughout the game, the player finds scrolls with spells composed of 6 different symbols which can be used my magicians. Most monsters and adversaries (mummies, trees, goblins, knights, dragons) making appearance in the game are also featured in the original Dungeon Master game, as well as the final boss. The dungeon structure has been conserved as well as some of the puzzles to be solved.
Dungeons & Dragons Collection: Tower of Doom

Dungeons & Dragons Collection is a two-disc compilation of Tower of Doom and Shadow over Mystara. It was released only in Japan on March 4, 1999, exclusively for the Sega Saturn. The ports have minor differences in gameplay, and there is a maximum of two players instead of the original four. Capcom originally planned to release Tower of Doom as a standalone title for the Sega Saturn and Sony PlayStation, but cancelled the plan early on. It was initially announced that the collection would be released for both the Saturn and PlayStation, with the PlayStation version due for a U.S. release, but the PlayStation version was never completed.

In 1999, James Mielke of GameSpot criticized the loading times as "horrendous", with mid-level battles occasionally pausing to let data stream in, and "as a very basic scrolling hacker", he called it simply "OK" and average. In 2005, IGN picked the Dungeons & Dragons Collection as one of the top ten co-op games.
DX Jinsei Game

DX Jinsei Game is a multiplayer party board game based on The Game of Life board game by Milton Bradley. The game features similar rules to the board game, though it is not a direct translation. Two to four players take turns spinning a roulette wheel to move forward on the board, and each space features various events; some will raise or lower the player's stats, some will allow the player to earn money, some are special events such as a first date or getting into college, and some contain mini-games. As the game progresses, each player progresses from high school through college, marriage, a career, starting a family, and finally retirement. The game ends once all players have reached the goal at the end of the map, and the player with the most money saved up is the winner.

The game offers three different courses, up to three computer-controlled opponents, and the ability to customize each player's avatar.
DX Jinsei Game II

DX Jinsei Game II is a multiplayer party board game based on The Game of Life board game, and a sequel to DX Jinsei Game. It is very similar to the previous release, again based on the board game but not a direct translation of any version, and the main differences are additional content as opposed to any mechanical changes.

Up to four players take turns spinning a roulette to move along the game board through each stage of their life, starting from infancy (as opposed to high school in the previous game) all the way through to retirement, with the winner being the player who gathers the most wealth. Each of the three maps this time features a theme — fantasy, travel across Japan, or the four seasons — and has a similar length. There are a large number of new events and mini-games compared to the previous release, and the game length can also be configured to allow for games as short as one hour.
DX Nippon Tokkyuu Ryokou Game: Let's Travel in Japan

DX Nippon Tokkyū Ryokō Game is a virtual board game in which the player travels by train around Japan visiting famous locations and tourist destinations. Each player is assigned a random "tour plan" which lists six locations around the country, and the goal is to visit as many of those locations as quickly as possible to see the sights. Each in-game day is divided into several turns: morning, day, afternoon, and evening; the player spins a roulette to determine how far they can move that that turn. Each station the player passes costs money, while reaching a destination will earn the player points and a money bonus; completing a full tour plan and returning to Tokyo will grant a large bonus. Various random events can also occur, such as finding a lost kitten or helping a pregnant woman reach a hospital, that may grant or lose points or money or give additional tasks for the player to do.
Earthworm Jim 2

Earthworm Jim returns in a madcap chase across the galaxy saving cows and thwarting lawyers all the way. Whip, run, jump and Snot swing your way through 10 of the most outrageous and untraditional levels anywhere. Returning favorite characters include; Princess What's-Her-Name, Psy-Crow, Peter Puppy, Bob the Goldfish, and several new villains as well!
Eberouge

Eberouge is a Japanese dating sim which is similar to Konami's Tokimeki Memorial. In a world called Worland where magic exists, players will spend a total of 5 years (2 years of primary school and 3 years at high school) as students who entered a magical school.

The core gameplay involves planning a weekly schedule, which includes school-related and free-time activities. Players have to arrange their daily classes and have a variety of things to study or practice including martial arts, science, literature, art, different kinds of magic, as well as go for extracurricular activities. All these classes influence the protagonist's statistics, making him attractive or vice versa to the various girls that he meets during his studies. The protagonist can also rest and travel to different places in the city.
Eberouge Special: Koi to Mahou no Gakuen Seikatsu

Eberouge Special: Koi to Mahō no Gakuen Seikatsu is a school life & love simulation game in the vein of Tokimeki Memorial, and an expanded and reworked version of Eberouge. This version of the game is significantly streamlined with the player starting as a new high school transfer student, removing the middle-school portion entirely and reducing the time limit to one year and nine months. Numerous new events have also been added, along with a new character, resulting in a much faster game with more events.
Eisei Meijin

Eisei Meijin is a digital conversion of the traditional Japanese board game Shogi for one or two players, and the first game in Konami's long-running Shogi series to come to console. In addition to standard play against the computer or a second player, it includes the ability to record and play back matches, and even includes playable records of several historical Shogi matches from the Edo era. Also included are a board edit mode and a tool that automatically solves Tsume Shogi problems.
Eisei Meijin II

Eisei Meijin II is a digital conversion of the traditional Japanese board game Shogi for one or two players, and the second game in the series to appear on consoles. It is very similar to the previous release, offering all of the same features: play against the computer or a second player, recording and playback of matches, playable records of historical matches, and a Tsume Shogi solver tool. New in this updated version of the game are:

• An improved move prediction tool with faster performance
• A new extra-easy "Level 0" difficulty option
• Additional historical matches available for replay
Eiyuu Shigan: Gal ACT Heroism

Eiyuu Shigan: Gal ACT Heroism differs in premise and structure from the vast majority of Japanese RPGs by focusing on non-linear questing rather than following a developed narrative. The game is set on a nameless island, which has elements of medieval fantasy as well as futuristic civilization. It allows the player to control a party of three female students from the School of Adventuring. The player can name the girls, but not change their unique battle techniques and proficiencies. The goal of the game is to reach a higher rank than the three competing teams (also containing girls only). Each team is accompanied by a guardian elf, and might also meet and/or hire other NPCs.

The game has an internal schedule, which reminds the player of the other competitors and what they might have accomplished in the meantime. Game progression is non-linear: the four cities on the island can be accessed right from the beginning.
Elevator Action 2 -Returns-

Elevator Action 2 -Returns- is Taito's sequel to their 1983 game. At the start of the game, you choose one of three characters, Kart Bradfield, Edie Burrett, and Jad the Taff. Each of them has their strengths and weaknesses, as well as different primary and secondary weapons. Your mission is to obtain the computer data that are hidden behind specially marked doors (colored red) in six buildings. Entering blue-colored doors during the game will trigger a spinning wheel that contains various items, and when you hit the fire button, what it stops on is what you get. These include point items, health items, machine guns, and rocket launchers. As with the original game, you can use elevators to travel between floors.

You can shoot various objects to destroy them, including barrels and drums, which can help defeat various enemies that include lackeys, zombie soldiers, karate agents, trench-coat goons, guard dogs, and more. Avoid being shot by these enemies.
Elf o Karu Monotachi

Elf o Karu Monotachi is an adventure game for Sega Saturn console based on anime with the same title. While the anime has been localized to Those Who Hunt Elves title in English-speaking countries, the game itself is Japan-exclusive release.

The story follows Junpei, Airi, and Ritsuko, who have been magically transported to fantasy new world. In order to return home, they have to find five spell fragments that have been placed on the skin of certain elves, which means in order to check which elf has the fragment they'll have to strip him or her naked. The story plays as a typical Japanese adventure game which feels like a visual novel with static backgrounds and characters, but also with a list of verb commands the player can click on each location (i.e. look, talk, move). The map shows each of the character and their locations and as the story progresses new locations become available.
Elf o Karu Monotachi II

Elf o Karu Monotachi II is a video-based visual novel-style adventure game based on the anime series known internationally as Those Who Hunt Elves. It is a direct follow-up to the first game, retelling the entirety of the show's second season. The player watches as the story proceeds in animated sequences taken directly from the TV show, and can occasionally make a choice between two options for which action the characters should take; this includes alternate sequences not found in the show. There are also occasional battle sequences which take the form of a slot-machine mini game.

The game also includes a bonus disc which contains interview clips with the voice cast, bonus voice clips, and a gallery of production artwork.
Elf o Karu Monotachi: Hanafuda-hen

Elf o Karu Monotachi: Hanafuda-hen is a hanafuda card game based on the anime series known internationally as Those Who Hunt Elves. It includes three different popular game types played with Japanese hanafuda cards: Koi-Koi, Hana-Awase, and Oicho-Kabu. The main story mode follows the cast as they challenge various elves to strip hanafuda in order to find the spell fragments they need that may be hidden on the elves' skin. There is also a free play mode, as well as a tutorial mode that teaches the basics of each game type to beginners.

The Saturn version features more revealing artwork for the female characters.
EMIT Vol. 1: Toki no Maigo

EMIT is a visual novel, divided into 3 parts, which was made to help Japanese people study English. The game can be played both in English or Japanese with the ability to listen to the audio and/or read the transcript in both languages. There are 2 modes to play the game: Story mode and English Game mode. The story mode is the main game divided into chapters where players get to watch the story unfold and can do a number of exercises after each chapter. During the story mode, players can pause the game at any time in order to look up a term they didn't understand or to change the language.

The exercises are:

• Listening comprehension activities where players pick the right options to check their understanding of the story.
• Guessing what's going to happen where players choose the question that's closest to their opinion and listen to the characters in the story commenting about the player's opinion.
EMIT Vol. 2: Inochigake no Tabi

EMIT is a visual novel, divided into 3 parts, which was made to help Japanese people study English. The game can be played both in English or Japanese with the ability to listen to the audio and/or read the transcript in both languages. There are 2 modes to play the game: Story mode and English Game mode. The story mode is the main game divided into chapters where players get to watch the story unfold and can do a number of exercises after each chapter. During the story mode, players can pause the game at any time in order to look up a term they didn't understand or to change the language.

The exercises are:

• Listening comprehension activities where players pick the right options to check their understanding of the story.
• Guessing what's going to happen where players choose the question that's closest to their opinion and listen to the characters in the story commenting about the player's opinion.
EMIT Vol. 3: Watashi ni Sayonara o

EMIT is a visual novel, divided into 3 parts, which was made to help Japanese people study English. The game can be played both in English or Japanese with the ability to listen to the audio and/or read the transcript in both languages. There are 2 modes to play the game: Story mode and English Game mode. The story mode is the main game divided into chapters where players get to watch the story unfold and can do a number of exercises after each chapter. During the story mode, players can pause the game at any time in order to look up a term they didn't understand or to change the language.

The exercises are:

• Listening comprehension activities where players pick the right options to check their understanding of the story.
• Guessing what's going to happen where players choose the question that's closest to their opinion and listen to the characters in the story commenting about the player's opinion.
Enemy Zero

Enemy Zero is one of the horror titles by Warp, closely connected to D (and its sequel D2 for Dreamcast). It also features the same heroine as in D series.

The crew members of the spaceship Aki were in a state of suspended animation. All of a sudden, the ship emergency program woke them up. What has happened? Apparently, a hostile alien life form had penetrated the spaceship. Now Laura, the heroine of the game, has to establish contact with her comrades, finding her way through the maze-like corridors of the giant vessel. She will also have to defend herself against the aliens, which seem even more intimidating because they are totally invisible.

The game consists of two genres: puzzle-solving adventure and shooter. When you enter a room, the enemies can't attack you, and you can explore it from 1st person perspective, taking objects, and solving puzzles. When you wander through ship corridors, you enter the 1st person shooter mode.
Eternal Champions: The Final Chapter

Eternal Champions: The Final Chapter was an unreleased game planned for the Sega Saturn by the former member of Sega of America, Michael Latham. The game only made it past the first 20 pages of concept art before being forcefully canceled by Sega of Japan, seeing the game as competition for the Saturn version of AM2's Virtua Fighter.

The Final Champter likely would have contained a second set of fighters fighting to regain their lives (called the Infernals), creating a balance to the timeline. A third force, called Chaos, would threaten the timeline and the two sides have to work together fight this new threat. Depending on your actions, the timeline would change, affecting the looks, abilities and histories of the characters in play. There were thirty planned possible endings.

While this third Eternal Champions game made it far into development before being axed, it is advertised on the box of early North American Sega Saturns for a release in Autumn 1995.
Eternal Melody

A regular young man is on his way home from school one day, and decides to take a shortcut through a construction site. Looking up, he sees a large steel beam hanging precariously... and then it suddenly falls straight down onto him! Fully ready in that moment to die, he instead finds himself in an unfamiliar world. He soon meets a fairy named Filly and a bard named Roxane, and is told that the only way to return home to his own world is with a special magic said to grant any wish; to find that magic, he'll need Filly's help to gather a group of companions. The two of them immediately set off to the nearest town to start their adventure...

Eternal Melody is a simulation adventure game similar to the better-known Yūkyū Gensōkyoku by the same developers. The main thrust of the game is to assemble a team of four party members and manage their schedules so as to improve their abilities and the protagonist's relationship with them.
EVE Burst Error

Eve burst error is set in modern-day Japan. The player controls two characters: a young, seemingly careless private investigator Kojiroh, and the special agent Marina. Kojiroh has been struggling to make a living as a lone PI, but now luck seems to smile to him: the director of the Eldian International School, Mr. Ko, asks him to find a missing painting, supposedly of great value. At the same time, Marina is hired by the ambassador of the fictional Middle East republic Eldia to protect his daughter Mayako from terrorists. Switching between Kojiroh and Marina, the player gradually finds out the connection between the two cases and plunges deeper into a mystery that involves political struggle, scientific discoveries, and horrifying murders.

The game is a traditional Japanese adventure: the player interacts with the world by choosing appropriate commands from the menu (which is different for every location).
EVE: The Lost One

EVE: The Lost One is a sequel to Eve burst error. The events of the game take place three years after those of the first game. The player is able to control two characters - the female detective Kyoko and the mysterious Snake, as they try to solve a complex mystery full of betrayals and political intrigues. In order to complete the game successfully, the player will have to to experience it from the perspectives of both heroes, helping each other to gather clues and to unlock events.

The game uses a menu interface typical for Japanese adventures. The player interacts with the game world by selecting menu choices, which mainly include looking, talking, or going to a different location. The game is done in anime style with characters appearing on still pre-rendered backgrounds.
Eyeful Home
Eyeful Home (アイフルホーム) is a piece of Japanese Sega Saturn software, containing an interactive tour of a house. It is one of the rarest Saturn "games" in existence.
F1 Challenge

F1 Challenge was the only Formula One title released on the SEGA Saturn, giving the player the opportunity to control five authentic Formula One cars and their drivers (Michael Schumacher, Damon Hill, Jean Alesi, Ukyo Katayama and Mika Häkkinen), with the ability to tweak their car before races, ranging from tire pressure, tire type, wing angle, etc.

There are six tracks to choose from: Hockenheim, Monte Carlo, Suzuka and three different configurations for a fictional track, Neo City, each with their own hairpin turns and fast straightaways. The player can choose from two behind the car views (no cockpit view is available) along with a pop-up screen that acts as a rear view mirror. Features a FOCA (Formula One Constructors Association) license which allows the use of thirteen teams with twenty-six drivers from the 1995 season from which the above mentioned five are the only ones playable.
Falcom Classics

Falcom Classics is a compilation of three classic games by Falcom for the Sega Saturn. Each game has been enhanced to take advantage of the superior specifications of the Saturn console, though their non-enhanced counterparts can also be played. Games included are: Dragon Slayer, Xanadu, and Ys.
Falcom Classics Collection
This compilation includes both volumes of the Falcom Classics remake collections, for a total of five games across two discs. The games come in two separate CD cases - one single and one double
Falcom Classics II

This is the second compilation of classic Nihon Falcom games redone for the Saturn. It contains remakes of:

• Asteka II
• Ys II

As before, all games feature newly remade graphics and music, as well as new gameplay features to counter the age of the gameplay mechanics in the games.
FantaStep

One day at a book shop, a young boy finds an old-looking picture book by the name of "Fantastep" that catches his eye. He buys the book and takes it home, but upon trying to read it finds that the stories and pictures are all mixed up. Also in the book are the words "Whoever has the courage to save the world in this book, sign here...", and as soon as the boy writes his name in the book, a ball of light envelops him and he awakens inside the world of the picture book. Now it's up to the boy to explore this jumbled-up fairy tale land, save the people within and solve their problems, and ultimately return back to his own world.

Fantastep is a point-and-click adventure game with 3D exploration; the player moves around in standard third-person action game style, but at any time can bring up a list of actions (such as examine, take, or talk to) and point at objects or characters to interact with them. The game world consists of small areas connected via a hand-drawn map of each region.
Farland Saga

Three warriors who were heading to the palace save the princess Fam from attackers. As they venture into the palace, they find out that a great hero who was trying to bring peace to the races of humans and magical people, was killed. Princess Fam is accused of murder. The three knights help her to flee the castle, but the ruler of magical people, Kaiser, declares war on humans. The runaway princess and her loyal knights find refuge in another country, and the inevitable war begins.

Farland Story is an anime-style tactical RPG. The game mainly consists of large strategic battles, during which you navigate your troops over an isometric battle fields, attack the enemies physically or cast spells. Terrain height plays a role in the battles, since some spells will only affect one level of terrain and one direction.
Farland Saga: Toki no Michishirube

Eight years have passed since the great war between humans and magical people. Brian, one of the war's great heroes, died peacefully, leaving behind the girl Kalin, of whom he had been taking care all the years following the war. Kalin leaves her country and goes on a ship to look for a job as a mercenary. On her way she meets Al, a boy who wanders around aimlessly, suffering from amnesia. Together, they reach a town where they receive jobs in the local guild. One of their assignments involves busting a pirate ship, and that is where their great adventure begins...

Toki no Michishirube is a direct sequel to the first Farland Saga game. It is an anime-style strategy RPG which consists mainly of large strategic battles, taking place on isometric battle fields. The player moves the characters over the battle field, attacking physically or casting spells. After a battle, characters gain experience points, which the player can freely distribute among the party members.
Farland Story: Habou no Mai

Farland Story: Habou no Mai is an independent side-story to the Farland Story series. The game is set in the same time line as the second and the third "mainstream" Farland Story games, 20 years after Arc has become a king. Peace has returned to the world, but on the continent of Ionia, an emperor is plotting an evil scheme. His son Riad refuses to accept the methods of his father, especially when he wants to use Serena, a girl he loves, for his plans of war and conquest. During a quarrel, Riad attacks the emperor's minister, and is forced to flee the castle together with Serena. The adventure of the runaway prince begins...

Graphically and gameplay-wise, the game is similar to other Farland Story games, although its setting is generally more dark. The game consists of large strategic battles, during which you move your party over the battle location, attacking enemies physically when they are in range of your weapons, and casting healing and offensive magic.
Father Christmas

Based on the British children's picture book written and drawn by Raymond Briggs and published by Hamish Hamilton in 1973. It's a point and click adventure game that features video from the 1991 animated film adaptation.
FEDA Remake! The Emblem of Justice

Feda Remake updates the original Super Famicom version of FEDA: The Emblem of Justice with a fresh coat of paint and some gameplay tweaks. Aside from its enhanced graphics and sound, this remake now also features fully animated and voiced cutscenes for key points in the story. While the gameplay is largely the same as the original, there are several noteworthy tweaks: the alignment system has been updated to make it more challenging to reach the absolute good or absolute evil alignments; some characters feature additional special abilities; and two new characters have been added, one for each alignment.
Ferox
Ferox is an unreleased puzzle game for the Sega Saturn. It does not appear to have been officially announced, however a prototype has since been unearthed and released online.
FIFA Soccer 96

FIFA Soccer 96 is a football (soccer) simulation. The game includes eleven leagues from all around the world, ranging from the unknown players of the Malaysian league to the celebrated stars of the English and Italian leagues. 59 International teams are also featured, and it's possible to match the teams you want to against each other through friendlies, or you can also choose to play domestic tournaments or International ones such as the World Cup. If you're not satisfied with the composition of the various teams, you can create your own dream team through the custom team creator.

British commentator John Motson comments all the incidents and happenings on the pitch in real-time. The ambient commentary is varied, and systems with more than the minimum memory level get extra commentary phrases. The Virtual Stadium technology has numerous pre-defined camera angles.
FIFA Soccer 97

FIFA Soccer 97 is the fourth game in the FIFA Series and the second to use the Virtual Stadium engine. Unlike the first game to use the engine, FIFA Soccer 97 features polygonal players as opposed to the 2D sprites used in FIFA Soccer 96. The engine however received complaints for being sluggish in the PC and PlayStation versions.

David Ginola (then a Newcastle United player) graced the cover of the game in the European market. He also was used for motion capture for the polygonal models in the game. Bebeto (the Brazilian striker) was featured on the cover for the Americas and Asia-Pacific markets.
FIFA: Road to World Cup 98

The late-1997 edition of FIFA was heavily tied in with the qualifying procedure for the 1998 World Cup. In the Road to the World Cup mode, you take a team from first qualification through to the main tournament, using the varying systems in different parts of the world. The game features 16 distinct outdoor stadia. The League play features 189 clubs and 11 leagues. Each team has specific crowd chants incorporated into the ambient sound.

The action is faster than in previous versions, and AI has been expanded. Players have distinct facial feature and hair styles. Each match is introduced by Des Lynam and commentated on by John Motson and former Scotland international Andy Gray.
Fighter's History Dynamite

The quest to defeat the mysterious Baron of Battlers, the mysterious K, is on. In order to get to this grotesque gladiator, however, you need to fight your way through 11 matches with the most skilled, most deadly of all combatants in the world of physical contact. Use your powers of pulverization, psychic energy blasts, and ridiculous strength to become the explosive fighting god in Fighter's History Dynamite!
Fighters Megamix

AM2's ultimate 3D fighting experience smashes onto the Saturn, with 32 characters from Virtua Fighter, Fighting Vipers, VF Kids, Sonic Fighters, Virtua Cop 2 and more! Secret characters, new weapons and new moves including many from VF3. The biggest and best beat-'em-up EVER!
Fighting Vipers

Electric fences. Barb wire cages. No-mercy skate punks. Axe-wielding rockers. Rollerbladers who take the term seriously... Fighting Vipers is street fighting in its rawest form. Furious, wall-to-wall combat brought to life with a visual intensity and relentless game play so superior, so brutal beyond comparison, nothing can prepare you for what you've got coming. NOTHING!
Final Fight Revenge

The Mad Gear gang is on the loose again! Take control of a total of 10 fighters (all from the original Final Fight) and foil them, making Metro City safe from crime once again.

Known as the last game released on the Saturn in Japan, Final Fight Revenge is a conversion of the arcade game (the only other Final Fight game released on that platform). As they battle 1-on-1 in a series of 3-D environments, one or two players control 10 characters from the original - the original three of Guy, Cody, and Haggar, plus enemy characters El Gado, Poison and Andore and four boss characters - Damnd, Sodom, Edi E. and Rolento.

In the single-player mode, the player fights through 6 opponents (followed by a final boss battle with a zombie version of the original Final Fight final boss Belger), armed with two punch buttons, two kick buttons and a special move button, which can used either to side-step (by holding while pressing up or down) or to pick up weapons and recovery items.
Find Love 2: Rhapsody

Find Love 2: Rhapsody is a love adventure game based on the Zenkoku Seifuku Bishōjo Grand Prix series of illustration collections. The protagonist is a high school student and aspiring musician who has been asked by his father to manage a condo building he owns in a resort town over the summer. This condo building just so happens to be the summer home of many beautiful young ladies from all over the country, and our hero hopes that he might, as the title suggests, find love with one of the ladies there.

The game is structured like other love simulation games such as Tokimeki Memorial, with the player improving various attributes and visiting various locations each day in hopes of meeting a particular girl. During conversations, the player can choose what tone to take, between normal, wild, and confident, which will affect that girl's reaction and affection level.
Find Love 2: The Prologue
Find Love 2: The Prologue (ファインドラブ２ ザ・プロローグ) is a 1998 multimedia disc released in Japan for the Sega Saturn by Daiki. It serves as a promotional disc for Find Love 2: Rhapsody, released later.
Fire Pro Wrestling S: 6Men Scramble

Fire Pro Wrestling S: 6Men Scramble is a pro wrestling game and part of the long-running Fire Pro Wrestling series. The arcade-style format is largely unchanged from previous entries; as the name suggests, the key new feature in this entry is 6-player simultaneous matches in both tag-team and battle royal formats.

Numerous game modes are available: Victory Road is the single-player campaign mode where the player must defeat a series of opponents to win the title belt; One Night Match is a standard exhibition match mode; Open League and One Night Tournament are tournament modes; and Elimination Match, Battle Royal, Death Match, and Gruesome Fighting are all special exhibition match types with specific rules or ring setups. The series' famously robust create-a-wrestler mode also makes an appearance, allowing the player to create completely custom wrestlers in both appearance and move set, which can then be used in any of the other game modes.
Fishing Koushien

Fishing Kōshien is a fishing game based on a TV show produced by TV Osaka. "Kōshien" refers to an annual high school baseball tournament held in Japan, and the show (and this game) adapts that format to fishing; eight high schools each send a team of three to enter a fishing tournament, and each round tasks the contestants with a different type of fishing. The game consists of four rounds: a black bass morning tournament, Kenzaki boat fishing, Japanese carp fishing, and Saipan big game fishing. Each round eliminates two teams from competition, and the goal is to be the winning team at the end of the competition.
Fishing Koushien II

Fishing Kōshien II is a fishing game based on a TV show produced by TV Osaka, and a follow-up to Fishing Kōshien. It features an identical format to the previous game: eight teams of three enter a fishing tournament, and each round challenges the player to a different kind of fishing. The four rounds consist of a black bass tournament, offshore boat fishing in Kenzaki, a carp relay race, and a big game survival match. Compared to the first game, the visuals have been revamped to use full-3D fish models rather than the 2D sprites of the original.
Fist

Fist is a 3D 1-on-1 fighting game in the tradition of Street Fighter II and a follow-up to Seifuku Densetsu: Pretty Fighter X, featuring several of the same characters. It uses a simple three-button fighting system — punch, kick, and guard — and includes story and 2-player versus modes, plus an arcade mode in the PlayStation version, with eight total characters to play as. Unusual for a game of its time, there is also a character bio mode which lets the player rotate and view the in-game character models from any angle.

Both releases of the game include a bonus disc with an audio drama and two music tracks.
Flash Sega Saturn: Ochikadzuki-hen

Flash Sega Saturn: Ochikadzuki-hen (フラッシュセガサターン おちかづき編) is a Japanese Sega Saturn demo disc. Unlike other Flash Sega Saturn series, this disc was bundled with the Saturn hardware.

Playable Demos included:
• Saturn Bomberman

Videos included:
• Cyber Troopers Virtual-On
• Sakura Taisen
• Tengai Makyou: Daiyon no Mokushiroku
Flashback: The Quest for Identity

You're Conrad B. Hart, Galaxis Bureau of Investigation Agent and right now you're stranded on a far-away planet after discovering an alien plot to overtake Earth. You must travel and find your way through four planets back to Earth and foil the aliens' sinister and deadly plans. This port is based on the famous Reminiscence.
Formula Grand Prix: Team Unei Simulation

Formula Grand Prix: Team Unei Simulation is a Formula One racing management simulation game. The player controls all the business aspects of running an F1 team, from hiring drivers and training the pit crew, negotiating with sponsors, and choosing parts and equipment for the team's car. The player manages their team through an annual series of 16-race seasons, with each race consisting of both a qualifier and a main race. Races are automated and not player-controlled but can be watched in real-time. Between races, the player can run tests to tune their equipment, train their pit crew to work faster, and use sponsor money toward developing better parts for their vehicle.

The PlayStation version of the game includes an official FOCA license and real names for many drivers and sponsors. The Saturn port lacks an official F1 license but adds the ability to customize the names. Both versions are otherwise nearly identical.
Formula Karts: Special Edition

Formula Karts is a semi-realistic racing title that attempts to capture the spirit of kart racing with it's low slung feeling of speed, and corner after corner of impressive handling (and inevitable sliding). The title supports both simulation and arcade modes, and features some effective race AI for non-player vehicles. Two player split screen is supported albeit with some slowdown.
Frank Thomas Big Hurt Baseball

Baseball player Frank Thomas licensed one of the first baseball games to use motion-captured 3D graphics and multiple camera angles. 28 stadia have been rendered in 3D, and each has its own visible and significant differences.

There are 6 distinct game modes, allowing for single exhibition matches as well as full seasons on the playoffs. There is also a Home Run Derby mode, allowing the player to pelt the ball out of the ground for points.

You can choose pitchers and batters, based on their statistics and form. Bowling options are set to define the delivery, with fastballs and curveballs as well as more precise setting of pace and height. Fielding is optional - it's best to leave this to the computer at first You can always alter the infield and outfield depth and shift.
Frankenstein: Through the Eyes of the Monster

This interactive movie puts a new twist on the Frankenstein tale: you are the monster! You have been falsely accused of murder and executed. However, the scientist Dr. Frankenstein (played by Tim Curry) has found a way to bring you back to life. You wake up in his laboratory, and your goal is to find out what exactly happened to you and what role Frankenstein played in your resurrection. Will you be able to return back to your former self?

The game plays entirely from first-person perspective. You wander around the huge laboratory, looking for clues and solving puzzles. Sometimes events will happen in the game, triggered by careful research of Frankenstein's notes and other clues. The game features live actors filmed over pre-rendered backgrounds.
Free Talk Studio: Mari no Kimama na Oshaberi

Free Talk Studio is an adventure-style game where the player takes the part of a radio talk show host interviewing various celebrities live on the air. Each week, the player has a choice of several guests such as an artist, a comedian, and a singer, and is presented with a short biography to review. At various points throughout the broadcast, the player must choose questions and responses from a list, which will affect the flow of the conversation and lead to different topics being discussed. The goal is to ask questions that will lead to the most interesting and engaging interview, and the player is graded at the end of each interview on the station's ratings for their show.

The Sega Saturn version of the game comes in two variants: the Red edition includes a behind-the-scenes booklet, while the Blue edition includes three trading cards featuring photos of the voice actresses.
Friends: Seishun no Kagayaki

Friends: Seishun no Kagayaki is a console port of an adult visual novel Dousoukai for PC. Sega Saturn port was released 3 years after the PC version and has all the adult content removed but is fully voice-acted. A PlayStation 2 port came 5 years after the Sega Saturn release in two versions, first one marked with age 18 restriction and second one a year later with age 15 restriction. Both PS2 versions, however, do not feature adult CG event scenes, but are fully voiced and have a new opening animation whereas Sega Saturn version does not feature an opening animation.

This is the first game in the Dousoukai series and starts with you on your way to a nice resort to reunite with some of your classmates from high-school. In particular, your tennis team members. The game focuses on romance and features full map of the place you're staying at as well as the rural town and its surrounding area.
From TV Animation Slam Dunk: I Love Basketball

Slam Dunk is based on the popular manga/anime of the same title, created by Takehiko Inoue. The game follows the story of Sakuragi Hanamichi, a high school delinquent, as he joins a basketball team in an attempt to win the heart of a young woman. The story follows the same plot as the anime/manga and progresses between basketball matches as you progress through the story mode.

Also available is a versus mode, where two players can play against each other using the pre-set teams or by mixing and matching players into their own personal dream team.
Full Cowl Mini Yonku Super Factory

Full Cowl Mini Yonku Super Factory is a racing management simulation game based on the Mini Yonku (Mini 4WD) line of toy cars produced by Tamiya and featuring characters from the Bakusō Kyōdai Let's & Go!! manga and anime by Tetsuhiro Koshita. In the main race mode, one or more players selects a car and a track, tunes 14 parts of their car based on a wide range of options, and then watches the race play out between a field of five computer-controlled racers. There is no direct control over the vehicles by the player. Up to five players can compete at once, and the game also includes a track editor.

This Special Limited Edition is the only release of the game, and includes a Gunbluster XTO Metallic Blue car model body plus a "Special Mini Book".
Funky Fantasy

Somewhere in the distant reaches of space, there exists a society where magic and technology coexist. In this world, peace is maintained by four great cards representing human emotions — Joy, Anger, Grief, and Pleasure. However, the Kingdom of Yoshimole, which protects the Card of Joy, has suddenly come under attack by the Rokuna Empire, which holds the Card of Anger, and strange monsters have appeared all over! The Queen of Yoshimole, Bunny Bee, escapes with her two retainers Riki and Alter, and together they must fight back against the Rokuna Empire and save their homeland.

Funky Fantasy is a comedy-fantasy turn-based strategy RPG. Many of the characters and situations are parodies of popular contemporary games and media, and the cast consists of comedians and actors from Yoshimoto Kogyo, the largest comedy talent agency in Japan at the time.
Funky Head Boxers

Funky Head Boxers is a slapstick boxing game adapted from the arcade game of the same title. This console conversion plays similar to the arcade version but includes significant changes and new content. Notably, the cast of boxers, originally consisting of Sega development staff, has largely been replaced with real-life comedians and actors represented by talent agency Yoshimoto Kogyo. This version includes a new "Champion Mode" in which the player selects a boxer and must train them to increase their stats by winning bouts. There is also a standard versus mode against either the computer or another player.

The Plus edition of the game, released several months later, includes the boss characters unlocked to play as by default and has various other minor polish but is otherwise identical to the original release.
Funky Head Boxers PLUS

Funky Head Boxers is a slapstick boxing game adapted from the arcade game of the same title. This console conversion plays similar to the arcade version but includes significant changes and new content. Notably, the cast of boxers, originally consisting of Sega development staff, has largely been replaced with real-life comedians and actors represented by talent agency Yoshimoto Kogyo. This version includes a new "Champion Mode" in which the player selects a boxer and must train them to increase their stats by winning bouts. There is also a standard versus mode against either the computer or another player.

The Plus edition of the game, released several months later, includes the boss characters unlocked to play as by default and has various other minor polish but is otherwise identical to the original release.
Fushigi no Kuni no Angelique

This game is a variation on the Angelique story: an ordinary school girl named Angelique becomes involved in a struggle to become the Queen of Cosmos, for which it is necessary to befriend the handsome and powerful Guardians of the Elements. The game features the same world and graphics as Angelique Special, with a slightly different story: Angelique falls asleep outside near a tree, and dreams that she fell through a rabbit hole (in an Alice in Wonderland fashion) into the magical land where she encounters her eternal rival Rosalia.

Unlike other Angelique games, Fushigi no Kuni no Angelique plays like a board game, with the kingdom divided into fields on which Angelique moves. There are no visible dice, but the amount of fields Angelique can walk on is determined randomly by clicking on the "move" button. Fields can either be empty, placed inside a location (like Angelique's own room), trigger events, conversations, etc.
Fuusui Sensei: Feng-Shui Master

Feng Shui is a traditional Chinese practice which posits that the physical layout of a landscape or other space determines how spiritual energy moves through it, in turn affecting the health and prosperity of that place and the people within.

Feng-Shui Master is an abstract simulation game based on that practice. Each stage consists of a city which the player can move around in first-person, filled with buildings, roads, and other structures and objects. Objects can be moved and adjusted, demolished and rebuilt, and the goal is to rearrange each area in accordance with Feng Shui practice in order to improve the city's prosperity and earn a certain amount of money. The player has a limited amount of money to make changes, but improving the energy flow and prosperity will increase the income and allow for further changes to be made. There are a total of seven stages, and the game also includes in-game book and video resources that explain the basics of Feng Shui.
G Vector

GVector is a sci-fi chase-view rail shooter in the style of Panzer Dragoon. The player pilots a small fighter craft and must fight off an alien invasion of Earth. There are two weapons at the player's disposal: a standard forward shot, and a homing laser that can lock on to up to eight targets; the more targets locked and destroyed simultaneously, the greater the bonus points awarded. There are a total of six stages, each with an encounter with a large boss enemy at the end, and the game includes a standard story mode as well as a score attack mode where any stage previously completed can be played and practiced for high scores.
Gaia Breeder

Gaia Breeder is a life-simulation sandbox game where the player attempts to recreate a natural environment. In the 23rd century, a meteor has wiped out all wild animal life on Earth, and humanity has decided to attempt to restore it using science. Using a time machine and a curious pink creature called "Mupi", the player travels back in time to harvest the DNA of extinct animals, then can clone or combine them in the present day. The game is divided into a series of "Breeder Tournaments" where the goal is to build a balanced and sustainable natural environment that can be used as a blueprint for restoring nature.
Gakkou no Kaidan

Gakkō no Kaidan is an interactive movie with adventure elements, made to tie in with a Japanese ghost-themed film of the same name. Like some other Sega CD games with similar thematics, it features FMV sequences with interactive options. For example, escaping some of the enemies may require the player to press directional keys or the A/C buttons. The other element of the game is a point-and-click style set.
Gakkou no Kowai Uwasa: Hanako-san ga Kita!!

Gakkō no Kowai Uwasa: Hanako-San ga Kita!! is based on the anime series of the same name. A group of curious children explore their school in the dead of night to check out the rumors of ghosts lurking about. They are rescued from certain dangers by the ghost girl Hanako. The game has the player move around in a 3D environment, navigating rooms and areas, solving puzzles, obtaining items and playing mini-games.
Gal Jan

Gal Jan is an arcade-style strip mahjong game. It is a standard 1-on-1 riichi mahjong game, and notably uses rotoscoped animation of real actresses for the opponents. The game features only a standard arcade mode where the player plays against each opponent in order. There are three opponents to face, who each progressively disrobe in animated sequences as the player wins matches against them. Gal Jan utilizes rotoscoping for its animation.
Galactic Attack

Galactic Attack is a top-down shooter, there are seven levels to play, ranging from battles in the atmosphere of planets to battling over mountain ranges, each with their own standard huge bosses at the end of each of these levels. The player takes control of a starfighter called the RVA-818 X-LAY, out to destroy any opposing forces.

The story has the future of Earth governments gathering together to construct a massive super computer called Con-Human to help with the planet's environment, providing nutrients to the earth and caring for the ecosystem. However, a cloned human is linked with the system and makes Con-Human a sentient being. The system eventually becomes insane and starts to create natural disasters, wiping all nearly all of mankind and destroying the ecosystem, driving the survivors into space to develop colonies on other planets.
Galaxy Fight

As the millennium nears in the far future, a being of ultimate power named Felden will make his appearance in the galaxy. It is unknown whether he comes to destroy all living beings or use his powers for good, but whatever the reason a group of skilled fighters from all corners of the universe have decided to beat each other up in order to face off against him and claim his power.

Enter Galaxy Fight, a one-on-one 2D fighter set in the far future and featuring sci-fi characters and settings. In the game itself, you have to select from 8 fighters, each with his unique moveset and stats, and then attempt to defeat the other character in 2 out of 3 matches using your special moves and attacks while avoiding your opponent's strikes.

Features single player and 2-player Vs. game modes, secret bosses and bonus rounds.
Gale Racer

Gale Racer is a 1st-person racing game where the scenarios are 2D and all of them correspond to 20 zones across the United States. The only available camera is the one inside the car, from where you can see the wheel and indicators (again, in 2D). Also, the game features weather effects, like rain, fog and night, for which you should use either the headlights or the windscreen wiper to succeed in the race.

The Saturn version is similar to the Arcade version except that your rivals are fully polygonal cars. It also adds Full Motion Video sequences, as well as a CD soundtrack.
Gals Panic SS

Gals Panic SS is the first game in the Gals Panic series designed specifically for home consoles. That said, there is no nudity. It is very similar to Gals Panic 4 before it in that all the girls are drawn in an anime style, with no photographic models whatsoever. The gameplay is changed in this game. The same basic gameplay of uncovering a girl's picture with Qix-like gameplay is used, but you spend 5 rounds on each girl. After this, instead of moving on to the next girl, the game saves and ends. You then play another girl after starting the game again. There is a gallery where the unlocked CG can be viewed. There are a total 12 models in the game, the last two unlocked after beating all the available girls. Some of these girls are reused from Gals Panic 4.
Gambler Jiko Chuushinha: Tokyo Mahjongland

Gambler Jiko Chuushinha: Tokyo Mahjongland is a riichi mahjong game based on the manga by Masayuki Katayama, and a sequel to Katayama Masayuki no Mahjong Dōjō. The game includes three different modes: the main Story Mahjong mode lets the player select either Hideyuki or Dorao and follows their visit to a strange mahjong-themed amusement park; Date Mahjong Anniversary mode lets the player pick from one of nine male characters and attempt to win the heart of one of 18 female characters by playing mahjong; and Free Battle mode is a standard match play mode where any of the 51 characters can be freely selected for a regular match.

Saturn version features completely redone graphics and sound, and includes an additional 5 characters in the free battle mode, but is otherwise the same game.
Game Basic for SegaSaturn

Game Basic for SegaSaturn lets you develop pieces of software on your Saturn. This is an updated Basic language with specific and powerful functions for the Saturn. You can develop some demos, games, tools, music and anything else you can think of! You can make 2D and 3D views with rotation and moves. You can make programs that will be compatible with any peripherals: control pad, mouse, virtua gun, multi-tap, 3D control pad, RAM cartridge,... You can import images and sounds directly.

With the serial cable provided, you can connect the Saturn to your PC (it works from Win95 to Win XP without any problems). With the help of the Basterm program, you can develop on your PC (which is really more comfortable), and then transfer your work to the Saturn directly. Saving your work is also easier on your PC than using the Floppy Disc Drive. One great feature is that you can use your PC keyboard to control Game Basic directly on the Saturn.
Game de Seishun

Game de Seishun is a multiplayer party board game in the mold of The Game of Life, which follows each player's avatar through five stage of youth, from kindergarten through to graduating high school and starting a career. The focus is on building friendship and relationships with various characters, and living a full and satisfying youth, with the winners being decided by so-called "seishun points" which are accrued by deepening interpersonal relationships, earning money from jobs, exercising and studying to improve oneself, and going on dates.

Each player moves through the board by selecting from one of several numbers to determine the number of spaces to move. Various spaces have different effects: some cause good or bad events to occur, some cause random events to happen, and some allow the player to pick a specific activity for the day such as studying or going to work which will increase various stats that in turn affect future events.
Game Nihonshi: Kakumeiji Oda Nobunaga

Game Nihonshi: Kakumeiji Oda Nobunaga is a historical simulation game with an emphasis on the "historical"; while similar to military strategy games such as Advance Wars, it is intended to teach real Japanese history through both the story and strategy gameplay. The game recreates 10 historical events of the life of Oda Nobunaga, from the battle of Iwakura Castle in 1558 through to his death in the Honnō-ji Incident in 1582, as turn-based strategy sequences in which the player controls Nobunaga and his troops, and must meet certain criteria to complete each mission. Animated sequences between each mission dramatize the events of the real historical figure's life.
Game no Tatsujin

Within Game no Tatsujin are four different classic Japanese board games made by different developers, which are Mahjong, Shogi, Go and Reversi. The board games can be played in three different modes including the Training Mode with five opponents, the Free Battle Mode with progressive levels of difficulty and World Mode with a total of 21 game masters to challenge with the ultimate goal beating them all and earning the award title "Master of the Game".
Game no Tatsujin 2

Game no Tatsujin 2 is a collection of digital conversions of seven board games popular in Japan: Shōgi, Igo, Renju, Mahjong, Chess, Reversi (called "Place" in this compilation), and Backgammon. Each game is a straightforward conversion of the real-world game, and includes a variety of configuration and difficulty options. All games other than Mahjong also include a two-player mode. In addition to the standard free mode, there is also a "Tatsujinsen" ("Master Battle") mode where the player can challenge masters of each game at the highest level of difficulty with a fixed set of rules.
Game no Tetsujin: The Shanghai

Game no Tetsujin: The Shanghai is a collection of three puzzle games which each make use of mahjong tiles:

• Shanghai, also called Solitaire Mahjong, in which the player must match tiles stacked in various grid patterns. Tiles can only be removed if they are fully visible (no tiles on top of them) and either the left or right edge is fully free.
• Rong Rong, also called Shisen-Sho, in which the player must match tiles stacked in various grid patterns. Tiles can only be removed if the matching pair can be connected by a line, with no more than two bends, which does not pass through any other tile.
• Shi-Kin-Joh, also called Forbidden City, a Sokoban-style block pushing game where the player must navigate a maze of oversized mahjong tiles to reach a goal. Pushing two matching tiles together will clear them from the board.
Game Tengoku: The Game Paradise!

Game Tengoku is a conversion of the coin-op game of the same name. The game is a vertical scrolling comical shooter similar to Konami's Parodius series and Hudson's Star Parodier.

The game is playable in normal or time attack mode.

The playable characters are:

• Jeynus Starmine, pilot of the Fighter-EX from Exerion
• Seria, pilot of the ship from Plus Alpha
• Z-DYNE MK II, the successor to the mech from Formation Z
• Pig, from Okkotoshi Puzzle Tonjan!?
• Momoko, from Momoko 120%
• Miki and Misato, two young girls piloting the radar ship Genesis 3 from Field Combat
Game-Ware Vol. 1

Game-Ware is a multimedia "digital magazine", and the first release in the quarterly series of the same title. This first volume includes several playable game demos and original minigames:

• Series of Dreams, a short branching text adventure where the player is a young man named Akira, who must make choices as he converses with two women: his girlfriend Shoko, and a mysterious girl named Megumi.
• Pipit Boy no Daibōken, a puzzle game where the player must guide a boy to collect all the gems on each stage; the boy follows whatever path he walks along, and the player rotates tiles to direct him around the map.
• Ejihon no Tantei Jimusho, a conversion of a "spot the different" style arcade game for up to four players where the player is shown an image filled with many kanji characters and must locate the one that does not match.
Game-Ware Vol. 2

Game-Ware Vol.2 is a multimedia "digital magazine", and the second release in the quarterly series of the same title. This volume includes several playable game demos and original minigames:

• Aoi Mizu no Naka, a suspense-horror adventure game with live-action video and photographs.
• Pipit Boy no Daibōken 2, a sequel to the puzzle game in the first volume in which the player must guide a boy to collect all the bones on each stage; the boy follows whatever path he walks along, and the player rotates tiles to direct him around the map.
• Telecom Town II, a simple side-scrolling shooter where the player shoots telephone cards as their projectile, and a sequel to the Nihon Telecom-sponsored game in the previous volume.
• Cinderella Cruising, a top-down driving game sponsored by Mitsubishi in which the player, just married and on the way home from their wedding, must drive their wife home in their brand new Mitsubishi Challenger SUV within a time limit.
Game-Ware Vol. 3

Game-Ware Vol.3 is a multimedia "digital magazine", and the third release in the quarterly series of the same title. As usual, this volume includes several playable game demos and original minigames:

• Ejihon, a "spot the different" style game for one or two players which returns from the first volume with new puzzle pictures, where the player is shown an image filled with many kanji characters and must locate the one that does not match.
• Onii-san, a simple point-and-click comedy adventure game.
• Pipit Boy no Daibōken 3, a continuation of the puzzle games found in the previous releases; the goal is still to guide the boy to collect all the objects on the screen, but it is now a falling-block puzzle game where two players compete to build a path for the boy.
• Protector Man: The King of Space, a simple Breakout-style game sponsored by razor company Schick.

Also included is a variety of multimedia content such as creator interviews, game previews, and an art gallery.
Game-Ware Vol. 4

Game-Ware Vol.4 is a multimedia "digital magazine", and the fourth release in the quarterly series of the same title. This edition is the first to come on two discs rather than just one, and includes significantly more content than previous volumes. As usual, this volume includes several playable game demos and original minigames:

• Pipit Boy no Daibōken 4, a continuation of the puzzle game series found in the previous volumes. This edition lets the player player Pipit Boy directly for the first time, as the game is now an auto-scrolling, top-down action game similar to Bump 'N' Jump, in which the player must collect small creatures to use as ammo while avoiding enemies and obstacles.
• Ejihon, a "spot the difference"-style game for one or two players in which the player is shown an image filled with many kanji characters and must locate the one that does not match; this version continues the story and contains new picture puzzles.
Game-Ware Vol. 5

Game-Ware Vol.5 is a multimedia "digital magazine", and the fifth and final release in the quarterly series of the same title. As usual, this volume includes several playable game demos and original minigames, with many ongoing series reaching their conclusion:

• Pipit Boy no Daibōken 5, the conclusion of the Pipit Boy series. This final edition takes the form of a simple action game where the player must target and reel in creatures and powerups while avoiding attacks, with the goal of reaching a quota before the other player.
• Ejihon, a "spot the different" style game in which the player is shown an image filled with many kanji characters and must locate the one that does not match; as usual, this version includes numerous new picture puzzles.
• The final chapter of Onii-san, a simple point-and-click comedy adventure game.
• Barbara Konomi's Sūsenjutsu, a numerology fortunetelling game.
Garou Densetsu 3: Road to the Final Victory

Fatal Fury 3 retains the format and controls of the previous game in the series, Fatal Fury Special. However, the two-plane battle stages have been revamped into a three plane format known as the Oversway System. The player fights primarily in the middle plane or the main plane, but can move or "oversway" into either of the sway lines at the background (LP+LK) or foreground (LK+HP). When the player performs an attack in a sway plane (or an Oversway Attack), their character will return to the main plane. Likewise, the player can attack an opponent who is in a Sway Plane with an Anti-Oversway Attack. The player can also do a "Quick Sway" to avoid an attack, leaving the opponent vulnerable to a regular attack.
GeGeGe no Kitarou: Gentou Kaikitan

GeGeGe no Kitarō: Gentō Kaikitan is a sound novel adventure game based on the long-running manga series originally created by Shigeru Mizuki. It's winter, and snow has started to fall in the forest where Kitarō and his friends live... but even during winter, snow never normally falls in their forest, and Kitarō worries about what this might mean. The game follows standard sound novel format, with unvoiced dialogue and narration over still images depicting the current scene, occasionally interrupted by choices which branch the story path. There are three main scenarios that can unfold — one in which Kitarō investigates the recent disappearance of bodies, one in which he investigates the source of the mysterious snow, and one in which a fake copy of Kitarō himself appears — each with multiple endings depending on the player's choices.
Gekiretsu Pachinkers

Gekiretsu Pachinkers is a gambling simulation game featuring both pachinko and pachi-slot (slot machine) games. It includes four playable machines of each type, which are original and not licensed from any specific real-life machines. The main story mode casts the player as an unemployed young man who decides to use the small amount of money he has left to take up gambling full-time and try to make it rich. The player sets either a time limit or money goal for the game and then must spend each day visiting the parlors and gambling to try to win as much money as possible. It's also possible to play the lottery, take out loans, and even go out in the evening looking for a date. In addition to the story mode there is also a practice mode where each of the eight machines can be freely practiced without any time or money restrictions.
Gekirindan: Time Travel Shooting

In 3195, Hokuto Higara, Shario Vissen, and their comrades join together in a fight against Huge Boss who has plans to render the human race extinct. To do this, the heroes will need to travel through various time periods in the past chasing down Huge Boss, whose disrupting human history.

Gekirindan is a vertical scrolling shoot-em-up. Players can choose from three different ship types (biplane, helicopter, and space fighter) to pilot, each equipped with their own unique firepower.. The game consists of 5 stages where the heroes travel through time from 3195 to 1942, 1999, 2373 and finally to 4580.

Some of the development team who helped create the game came from the recently defunct at the time Toaplan, hence the game sharing similarities to that companies previous shoot-'em-up efforts.
Gekitotsu Koushien

Gekitotsu Koushien is a super deep high school baseball tournament simulator. Like the Little League World Series, in Japan Koshien is a huge tournament. With over 4000 teams involved (and all of that data put into this game!) it is a great place for scouts to find professional players, and the game is a great and totally unique baseball experience.
Gekka no Kishi: Ouryuusen

Gekka no Kishi: Ōryūsen is a digital conversion of the traditional Japanese board game shogi for one or two players, based on the manga series Gekka no Kishi by Junichi Nojo. The main story mode follows protagonist Shosuke Himuro as he battles through a shogi tournament against each of the other opponents. There are also practice and jōseki modes, as well as a free battle mode for one or two players where any of the characters can be selected. The practice and free battle modes include a range of rule configuration options.
Gensou Suikoden

Loosely based on the classic medieval Chinese novel Water Margins, the game is a fantasy RPG set in an imaginary universe, its main theme being political struggle. The hero of the game is the young son of Theo McDohl, a general who serves the Scarlet Moon Empire, presently controlling the land of Toran. Through a series of events the hero becomes involved in a rebellion against the Empire, led by an organization known as the Liberation Army. Will the hero find a new home there, will he be able to tear himself away from everything that has been sacred to him, including his own father?

Suikoden is a Japanese-style role-playing game with several unusual additions. There are three kinds of combat in the game, the most common one being the traditional turn-based party combat (players can have up to six people in their active party). Magic runes can be equipped on the player's characters which allow limited usage of offensive and healing spells.
Gex

GEX's mouth gets him in trouble, but it's his thrashing tail and suction cup paws that get him out. GEX has been sucked into the Media Dimension, the place where cheesy 70's movies go to retire. To escape he's gotta kill TVs in each world. Over 450 frames of smooth 3D animation and hand-rendered backgrounds! GEX jumps and sticks to everything while thrashin' secret levels in search of elusive remote controls.
Ghen War

Ghen War is a classic first-person shooter. The solar system is being attacked by an evil force of aliens known as Ghen. The player is a Lieutenant surface engineer in a hypersuit, and it is his task to boot these aliens out of your world in twenty levels. From the cockpit of this hypersuit, the character operates lasers, grenades, mines, missiles and more while making his way across planet surfaces and city environments protecting the human race. It also has a claw that can operate elements in the environment and can send out a decoy of itself to confuse opponents.

The game is also one of the first to feature deformable terrain. Explosions make craters and firing into the environment can make it wear away.
Ginga Eiyuu Densetsu

Ginga Eiyū Densetsu is a strategy simulation game, and part of a long-running series based on Yoshiki Tanaka's Legend of the Galactic Heroes science fiction novels. This console version is most similar to Ginga Eiyū Densetsu III, with the player taking the role of a top general in either the Galactic Empire or the Free Planets Alliance, commanding an entire fleet of ships. The game is divided into two main sections. In the strategy sections, the player is shown a full-scale map of the conflict, showing planets and the locations of ships; here the player may direct ships to move or engage with enemies, as well as converse with their officers. When battle starts, the player controls their fleet from a top-down perspective in semi real-time; each vessel can be given orders which they will carry out as instructed, but the action can also be paused at any point to issue new orders.
Ginga Eiyuu Densetsu Plus

Ginga Eiyuu Densetsu Plus is a revised and expanded edition of the previous Sega Saturn entry in the long-running franchise, featuring several changes and new additions:

• A new scenario mode featuring four campaigns, smaller in scope than the main game
• Additional story event scenes featuring the voice cast from the anime
• Various tweaks to the game mechanics such as a more restricted ability to resupply ships, resulting in a generally more difficult game
Ginga Ojousama Densetsu Yuna 3: Lightning Angel

Yuna and her friends are enjoying a relaxing day shopping when suddenly an intergalactic army appears with plans of conquering the Earth. With the fate of the planet on the line, Yuna and her rivals must put aside their differences and fight back against this intergalactic menace.

Ginga Ojōsama Densetsu Yuna 3: Lightning Angel is the third mainline game in the Galaxy Fräulein Yuna series. Gameplay is very different from prior entries in the series; while story sequences are presented in the same digital-comic format as the previous games, this time the battle sequences take center stage and are presented as isometric turn-based strategy battles in the vein of Tactics Ogre. The player can control a team of up to eight characters depending on the scenario, and each character has their own abilities and special techniques. Choices made during the adventure sequences can also affect the particular conditions of the following battle.
Ginga Ojousama Densetsu Yuna Mika Akitaka Illust Works

Ginga Ojousama Densetsu Yuna Mika Akitaka Illust Works (銀河お嬢様伝説 ユナ あきたか みか イラストワークス) is an art gallery for the Sega Saturn.

It was followed by Ginga Ojousama Densetsu Yuna Mika Akitaka Illust Works 2.
Ginga Ojousama Densetsu Yuna Remix

Yuna Remix is a remake of the original PC Engine game. The gameplay and story are identical to the original release, but this version features completely redrawn graphics at a higher quality, newly-arranged music, and additional newly-recorded voiceovers. There is also some additional bonus content such as an illustration gallery. The package also includes a 1997 calendar featuring new artwork by series illustrator Mika Akitaka.
Ginga Ojousama Densetsu Yuna: Mika Akitaka Illust Works 2
Ginga Ojousama Densetsu Yuna Mika Akitaka Illust Works 2 (銀河お嬢様伝説 ユナ あきたか みか イラストワークス 2) is an art gallery for the Sega Saturn and "sequel" to Ginga Ojousama Densetsu Yuna Mika Akitaka Illust Works.
Girl Doll Toy: Tamashii o Kudasai...

Girl Doll Toy is a love adventure game centered around a female android. The protagonist is a young college student working part-time at a laboratory that develops humanoid androids. Following a failed experiment, he takes home an android slated for disposal, fixes and upgrades her back into working order, and gives her the name Erika. While at first Erika is only able to directly obey commands, with the player's help she will gradually learn independent thought, emotion, and eventually even love.

The game plays in standard Japanese-style adventure format, with voiced dialogue and limited interaction through simple commands like talk and move.
