Metal Black is an arcade 2D side-scrolling shoot'em up, made as continuation of Final Gun Frontier" and Darius. Aliens (called Nemesis) invaded Earth, won the war, and took most of the raw materials and the player, piloting a spaceship, fights against those aliens. His vehicle is the CF-345 Black Fly, and he must "fly right, and shoot enemies". He has only 1 weapon, and collects special pickups to increase firepower (and activate power-beam). The game has 6 levels & 2 bonus levels, each with their own song.
Metal Fighter Miku

In the year 2061, technological advancements have allowed humans to surpass the limits of the weak human body. A new form of entertainment called Neo Pro Wrestling, which allows combatants to use powered armor and other enhancements, is rapidly gaining in popularity. The Pretty Four are a team of teenage wrestlers/pop idols, riding high after their newest member, Miku, snatched a world championship victory. Suddenly, a new tournament is announced by a mysterious new group called The Lion's Den, and Miku and the Pretty Four decide to take on the challenge.

Metal Fighter Miku is a Japanese-style adventure/simulation game based on the 1994 animated series of the same name. It features a new scenario in six chapters set six months after the events of the show, essentially functioning as a sequel. The player controls Miku and must develop her abilities and ultimately win each match as the story progresses.

The game is divided into two main sections.
Metal Slug

Metal Slug, originally released on the Neo Geo, is a side-scrolling shoot'em'up.
The player(s) takes the role of a soldier (or two) and fights a gigantic army. Every level consists of running forward blasting anything that moves, while collecting power-ups along the way (there's also a wide selection of weaponry in the game). In the end of each level the player goes up against one gigantic boss.
Mezase Idol Star!! Natsuiro Memories: Mahjong-hen

A television station is holding tryouts to find a new pop idol to represent the company. After several rounds of auditions, only eight young women remain in the running. The final test, to determine both their intelligence and luck, is a mahjong tournament! Whoever wins the tournament also wins the audition, and the competition is fierce.

Mezase Idol Star!! is a 1-on-1 mahjong game featuring a cast of aspiring young idols, each portrayed by a real-life actress. The player takes the part of a manager and selects a girl to represent in the tournament; to win the audition, the player must defeat all seven of the other girls at mahjong. The game also includes profiles and a photo gallery of each girl, and additional swimsuit photos are unlocked after clearing each girl's scenario.
Midway Presents Arcade's Greatest Hits

Midway Presents Arcade's Greatest Hits is a compilation that includes the following games:

• Bubbles
• Defender
• Defender II
• Joust
• Robotron: 2084
• Sinistar
Mighty Hits

Mighty Hits is a shooting gallery game and the gameplay and stages are very similar to Point Blank in theme and presentation. The game has a cartoony wild west theme throughout the cut scenes and menu screens.

One or two players compete in a series of mini games, which last about 20 or 30 seconds each. The rules of the mini games are displayed before each round. In general players have complete objectives and puzzles by shooting at targets. After each round a results screen shows if the objectives were completed or failed. Failing a round and the player loses a life feather, lose all feathers and the game is over.

There are 3 courses to select from, represented by a blue, green and yellow tin can. There is Easy (6 mini-games), Medium (9 mini-games) and Hard (15 mini-games) and completing hard mode unlocks a black tin can for Very Hard with 18 mini-games. The game is played in sets of 3 stages, the player has to shoot 3 cards to select the stages.
Minakata Hakudou Toujou

Minakata Hakudou Toujou is mystery adventure game with a faux claymation visual style. The player takes the role of an assistant to the titular Inspector Minakata, reviewing footage of crime scenes to look for anything suspicious. The bulk of the player's interaction involves clicking on objects, which will trigger dialogue descriptions of the object and ultimately lead to the solution of each case. The game includes two short tutorial cases and two longer main story cases.
Minami no Shima ni Buta ga Ita: Lucas no Daibouken

While searching for food for his village, the pig Lucas climbed a huge tree in hopes of stealing the eggs from a giant bird's nest. However, when he reached the nest, the mother bird saw him and chased him away. Upon returning to his village in defeat, Lucas finds all the homes ransacked and everyone gone but one young piglet, who is snatched away by a bird right before his eyes. Lucas sets out to rescue the piglets, and his journey will take him all across the island.

Minami no Shima ni Buta ga Ita: Lucas no Daibouken ("There was a Pig on the South Island: Lucas' Great Adventure") is a puzzle game featuring an assortment of logic puzzles. The game is divided into six themed worlds, and each world is divided into six levels in two types. Even-numbered stages are simple platform action sequences where Lucas can jump and use a whip to attack, avoiding enemies and looking for piglets to rescue.
Minnesota Fats: Pool Legend

Minnesota Fats: Pool Legend is a pool game where the player can participate in a story mode and play against a set of pros in six different pool halls in an attempt to face off against Minnesota Fats himself. There are seven different variations of pool to play: Eight-Ball, Nine-Ball, Rotation, 14-1 rack, Three ball, Cut Throat & One Pocket. There is also a Versus Mode to let players take on any opponent of their choice including a two-player option to take on a friend and a Tournament Mode. Players can also try out the Trick Mode that has the player try to compete 16 different trick shots.
Minton Keibu no Sousa File: Doukeshi Satsujin Jiken

Minton Keibu no Sousa File: Doukeshi Satsujin Jiken is a murder mystery adventure game, and a full remake of Thinking Rabbit's 1985 release Doukeshi Satsujin Jiken. The game is set in Brighton, England in 1932 at a traveling circus; the protagonist, Detective Frank C. Minton, is sent from London to investigate after a clown is found dead. The player, as Detective Minton, must explore the circus and nearby town searching for evidence and questioning suspects. Of particular note is that the player can change the tone of questioning with suspects, choosing to be gentle, firm, or harsh depending on the circumstance.

Compared with the original game, there are numerous changes and upgrades. Notably, the text parser interface has been replaced with a simplified command menu. All environments are pre-rendered in full 3D, while characters are presented as 2D illustrations with full voice acting.
Mizubaku Daibouken

In Mizubaku Daibouken, you play Hipopo the Hippopotamus who must venture through a large number of enemy-packed levels in search for his missing girlfriend, as well as rescuing other hippo-like creatures along the way. The game features moving platforms, collapsible floors, boats, water-wheels, and plants that can be watered, causing them to grow and allowing you to reach much higher platforms.

Hipopo is supplied with magical water globes, which can be thrown at enemies to freeze them. Once frozen, the enemies can be kicked and destroyed completely. If idle for a few seconds, enemies will unfreeze themselves and continue their business. Every two levels is a boss that needs to be defeated in order to proceed to the next one.
Mizuki Shigeru no Youkai Zukan: Soushuu-hen

Mizuki Shigeru no Youkai Zukan: Soushuu-hen is a Japanese-style adventure game plus a multimedia database of youkai (spirits and ghosts of Japanese folklore) featuring illustrations and commentary by youkai scholar and GeGeGe no Kitarou creator Shigeru Mizuki. The database portion collects together the contents of three prior PC releases with information on a total of over 950 different youkai.

In the game section, the player has come to Mizuki-sensei's home to become his disciple, but he has gone missing. The player visits various locations to search for the missing professor, and encounters many different youkai in combat along the way. Combat is non-traditional; rather than attacking them directly, the player must use their knowledge of the various spirits to select the correct action or response to safely ward them off.
Mobile Suit Gundam

Mobile Suit Gundam is a side-scrolling action game based on the popular 1979 animated series of the same title and its three film adaptations, casting the player as the series' main character, the young pilot Amuro Ray. The story generally follows the plot of the films with only minor changes, and includes new animation from the original animation studio Sunrise that remakes famous scenes from the original.

The player pilots the titular RX-78-2 Gundam in both ground-based run-and-gun and space-based flight stages, using various weapons to destroy enemies; Radio chatter from other characters plays throughout each stage, and it is often necessary to destroy all enemies in an area to advance the story. As missions are completed, additional weapons become available and the player can customize their equipment loadout before each stage.
Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story I: Senritsu no Blue

Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story I: Senritsu no Blue is a first-person action shooting game based on the popular Mobile Suit Gundam media franchise. Relatively unique among Gundam games, it tells an original story not adapted from another media, and is the first in a three-part trilogy. It is set during the One Year War, shortly after Operation Odessa; the player controls Earth Federation pilot Yuu Kajima, who alongside his teammates Philip Hughes and Summona Fulis are sent on missions with experimental Mobile Suits in order to collect data for production. The team encounters a mysterious blue Mobile Suit that seems bent on eradicating Yuu's team, and which seems to show up without warning.

The game is divided into five missions, each of which has specific objectives such as destroying a particular target or defending a specific structure or character. The story is told through radio communications during gameplay, and objectives may change as the mission progresses.
Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story II: Ao wo Uketsugu Mono

Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story II: Ao o Uketsugu Mono is a first-person action shooting game based on the popular Mobile Suit Gundam media franchise. Relatively unique among Gundam games, it tells an original story not adapted from another media, and is second entry in a three-part trilogy, following after Senritsu no Blue. It once again casts the player as pilot Yuu Kajima, with the identity of the mysterious blue MS starting to be revealed.

The game is again divided into five missions, each of which has specific objectives such as destroying a particular target or defending a specific structure or character. The story is told through radio communications during gameplay, and objectives may change as the mission progresses. There are no branching story paths or loadout customization, though the player is ranked at the end of each mission which has an effect on the overall ending. Save data can be carried over from the first game, and into the third after completing all missions.
Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story III: Sabakareshi Mono

Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story III: Sabakareshi Mono is a first-person action shooting game based on the popular Mobile Suit Gundam media franchise. Relatively unique among Gundam games, it tells an original story not adapted from another media, and is third and final entry in a three-part trilogy, following after Ao o Uketsugu Mono. This concluding chapter once again has the player controlling pilot Yuu Kajima. Two machines remain with the experimental EXAM System, designed to mechanize the abilities of Newtypes and allow human pilots to have the same capabilities: one has been stolen, purportedly by the pilot of the mysterious blue MS, Efreet; the other has been assigned to Yuu.

The game is again divided into five missions, each of which has specific objectives such as destroying a particular target or defending a specific structure or character. The story is told through radio communications during gameplay, and objectives may change as the mission progresses.
Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story: The Blue Destiny

Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story: The Blue Destiny collects together all three Saturn Gundam Side Story releases in a single package:

• Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story I: Senritsu no Blue
• Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story II: Ao o Uketsugu Mono
• Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story III: Sabakareshi Mono

Also included is a bonus "Optional Guide" disc which includes an illustration gallery and play videos of each mission, as well as a set of trading cards.
Momotarou Douchuuki

Momotarou Douchuuki is a multiplayer board-game and a spinoff of Hudson's Momotarou Dentetsu series. It features many of the same characters and gameplay elements as the main series games, but with a new setting in the Edo period of Japanese history. As with other Momotetsu games, players take turns moving around the board via dice rolls, acquiring property to earn money, trying to avoid giving money to other players, and encountering a wide variety of random (and often comical) events that can grant each player various benefits or handicaps.
Monster Slider

Monster Slider is a falling-block puzzle game similar to Columns or Puyo Puyo. Colored blocks fall in pairs from the top of the screen and must be arranged to match 3 or more of the same color together. Uniquely the entire playfield is at a tilt, causing blocks to slide to one side to fill gaps when they are placed or after clearing other blocks; the player can reverse the tilt at any time, causing blocks to slide in the opposite direction. Combos will launch garbage blocks at the opposing player, and if the blocks reach the top of the well that player loses the round. Each character also has a unique special ability.

The main single-player story mode casts the player as a young woman named Nina whose sister has been kidnapped by Count Dracula; she must defeat each of Dracula's minions and eventually Dracula himself in order to rescue her. There is also a two-player versus mode and a single-player endless mode.
Moon Cradle

Moon Cradle is a mystery adventure game which uses live-action video for cut-scenes and fixed isometric perspective during actual gameplay. The player controls the character directly while actions such as "search", "talk" or "use" are presented in a menu-selected manner.
Mortal Kombat II

Following his failure to defeat to Liu Kang in the first Mortal Kombat game, the evil sorcerer Shang Tsung begs his master, Shao Kahn, to spare his life. He tells Shao Kahn that the invitation for Mortal Kombat cannot be turned down, and if they hold it in Outworld, the Earthrealm warriors must attend. Kahn agrees to this plan, and even restores Tsung's youth. He then extends the invitation to Raiden, who gathers his warriors and takes them into Outworld. The new tournament is much more dangerous, as Shao Kahn has the home field advantage, and an Outworld victory will allow him to subdue Earthrealm.
Mortal Kombat Trilogy

All the characters from the first three Mortal Kombat games return for the ultimate battle. You can play as Kano, Reptile, Mileena, Kung Lao, Shang Tsung, Sindel, Sketor, Stryker, Nightwolf, Sheeva, Kitana, Scorpion, Sonya, Smoke (Cyber Ninja), Rain, Jade, Baraka, Johnny Cage, Ermac, Noob Saibot, Sub-Zero (Unmasked), Sub-Zero (Classic), Jax, Rayden, Cyrax, Liu Kang, Smoke (Human), Kabal, Goro, Kintaro, Motaro, or Shao Kahn.

This game is one-on-one martial arts fighting. The player can choose from over thirty different characters, all with their own fighting style and their own special moves. Trilogy differs from the other games in that you can play combinations of people that otherwise isn't possible, such as old Liu Kang vs. new Liu Kang, etc.
Motteke Tamago with Ganbare! Kamonohashi

A platypus family accidentally loses their eggs so the father must go out and retrieve them from the river. Turns out it won't be that easy since a duck picks up the eggs so they have to fight over who owns the eggs. After defeating the duck the eggs keep rolling off to another animal over and over again. Will they ever return home? 

Motteke Tamago with Ganbare! Kamonohashi is a top-down Bomberman-style multiplayer arcade action game, and an enhanced port of the PC Engine game Motteke Tamago. This version includes the same arcade mode as the original release, and also adds a single-player story mode with multiple stages and new creatures to play as other than ducks, such as frogs and platypus.

Playing as one of a cast of cute characters the player will move around a arena collecting eggs and dash attacking into opponents. The dash attack will cause the opponent to drop all their eggs.
Moujiya

Take Money Puzzle Exchanger, sprinkle on some Puyo Puyo, and what do you get? Hey presto, it's Moujya! Players control falling pairs of yen coins, in assorted denominations from 1 through 500. Making change by combining coins into the amount of a higher denominations combines the set of coins into one coin of the larger size, and combining two 500 yen coins makes them disappear. Efficient coin placement can lead to making large combos by letting transformed coins fall into place to make change for a higher denomination.

This rendition of Moujya gives the original game a bright and colourful makeover and replaces the cast with cute cats.
Mouri Motonari: Chikai no Sanshi

Mouri Motonari: Chikai no Sanshi is a tactical RPG in the vein of Shining Force. It is a historical drama based on the life of 16th-century daimyo Mouri Motonari, and the third entry in Koei's Eiketsuden series of historical RPGs. The story opens in 1517 with Motonari forced to take the reins of his clan following the deaths of both his father and elder brother.

The game is split into 27 chapters which each opens with a story event, then allows the player to speak with advisors and villagers as well as to prepare for the next battle. Villagers may have various requests, which when completed will reward the player with equipment or new recruits for battle. Additionally, equipment can be upgraded and soldiers can be trained at this time. Battles take the form of a top-down turn-based tactical format, with individual units engaging 1-on-1. Each battle has specific win conditions, and the story is linear with no branches.
Mr. Bones

Assume the role of Mr. Bones, a dead blues musician resurrected from his grave who finds himself part of DaGoulian's evil army of darkness. Battle this army of darkness before it succeeds in spreading evil throughout the world! Drop-dead, never-before-seen animation. Original music by blues' guitarist Ronnie Montrose. Revolutionary real-time shadows and story telling. Over 20 marrow-tingling levels of unique gameplay.
Mujintou Monogatari R: Futari no Love Love Island

Mujintou Monogatari R: Futari no Love Love Island is a survival simulation with love adventure elements, and part of the Mujintō Monogatari series. The protagonist is on a Hawaii vacation, but winds up stranded on a deserted island with five other vacationers: four female and one male from a total of 10 possible, with the specific companions selected by the player's choices in the introduction. The player must guide their group to work together to survive, and ultimately figure out a way off the island within three months, while also pursuing a romantic relationship with one of their companions.

The player's group is divided into three pairs, and the player can give each group instructions for both the morning and afternoon of each day, including to explore or investigate locations looking for resources, prepare food, or to rest.
Murakoshi Seikai no Bakuchou Nihon Rettou

Murakoshi Seikai no Bakuchou Nihon Rettou is a fishing game featuring professional fisherman and author Seikai Murakoshi. The game includes a total of 11 locations from all across Japan to fish at, and each location has a specific target fish and quota to meet. Completing a stage will move on to the next, with the final stage being a 1-on-1 challenge against Murakoshi himself. Between stages, the player can use points earned from catching fish to obtain new rods and lures. There are also advice videos featuring Murakoshi giving beginner and intermediate fishing advice for the player.
My Best Friends: St. Andrew Jogakuen-hen

My Best Friends: St. Andrew Jogakuen-hen is a anime-style jigsaw puzzle game with mild erotic content. The player meets up with various pretty young ladies at their school, attempting to woo them with jigsaw puzzle prowess. Each of the eight girls has multiple snapshots that appear as a puzzle, and completing the puzzle will reward the player with an animated scene of that girl; if the player can complete the puzzle quickly enough, the animated scene will show the girl topless, and the player will also get that girl's phone number to view the scene again. After gathering all eight phone numbers, an additional topless puzzle image is unlocked for each of the girls.
My Dream: On Air ga Matenakute

My Dream is an simulation game focusing on the world of voice-actors. There are eight different heroines in the game, and each has been voiced by three different actresses. Voice actress for each heroine can be set up at the beginning of a new game, right after entering the player's name. The game doesn't feature default name for the player, and other characters will address you by the name you enter (both Japanese and Latin letters are available during name creation). The player focuses on a single heroine and by setting up a weekly schedule for her, the game advances as a visual novel with selectable dialogue and action choices at certain locations and during certain conversations. The weekly schedule is set by selecting locations on the map you wish to visit, one location per day. Different location offer different actions and participation in various events and meeting and talking to other characters.
Myst

You have just stumbled upon a most intriguing book, a book titled Myst. You have no idea where it came from, who wrote it, or how old it is. Reading through its pages provides you with only a description of an island world. But it's just a book, isn't it? As you reach the end of the book, you lay your hand on a page. Suddenly your own world dissolves into blackness, replaced with the island world the pages described. Now you're here, wherever here is, with no option but to explore.

Myst is a first-person point-and-click adventure where the player controls a character known as The Stranger. Magically transported into the world described in the book, he needs to explore Myst Island and solve its mysteries. The game is presented as a series of static scenes where the player acts with the environment by clicking and manipulating objects. There are no enemies and it is not possible to die.
Nanatsu Kaze no Shima Monogatari

Nanatsu Kaze no Shima Monogatari, roughly translated by the developer as “The Seven Blasts of Wind in Island Story” (but better translated as “The Tale of Seven Winds Island”), is a commonly neglected masterpiece released by Enix exclusively for the Saturn in 1997: one that didn’t obtain the same accolades as other RPG and Adventure titles released for this system. As a two CD set, the game was accompanied by a Premium disk that featured some of the most beautiful matte art ever conceived for a video game, along with singular item and character designs. Essentially, Nanatsu Kaze no Shima Monogatari is an interactive storybook whose illustrated chapters reflect the game’s very own narrative, with a new chapter being added every time the player successfully completes a group of tasks.
Nanatsu no Hikan

In this mystery adventure game, a young man called Ippei has been given the key to the seven mansions his uncle wants to restore and turn into a resort. But these mansions were never fully explored and his uncle suspects a great treasure to be hiding somewhere on the premise, and Ippei is tasked to look into it. However, he is warned that there may be dangerous people lurking around. The game uses 3D graphics and a first-person perspective to let the player full explore the mansion up close. The more Ippei explores the mansion, the more he will find out about his family's history. Ippei can pick up and use various items, talk to other characters or simply think out loud to give clues to the player. While there are no action elements, the protagonist has a health bar which can be decreased if he is not careful and activates various traps that lie hidden throughout the mansions.
NASCAR 98

With top-of-the-line racing simulation NASCAR 98 allows you to race with 24 drivers including legend Dale Earnhardt and 10 official tracks and extra 6 fantasy tracks. This NASCAR game allows you to hear all screeching burnouts, oiled skids, and emergency vehicles, or listen to provided music. This includes the modes season, Arcade, and new custom racing(control opponents,laps,gas gauge, and just about anything.).
NBA Action

TAKE IT TO THE HOLE!

• All 29 NBA teams
• Over 400 NBA players
• Monster surround sound
• Sweet 360° camera angles
• Radical playing views
• Season stat-tracking
• In-depth playbooks for offensive and defensive plays
• User records
• Player attributes in more than 20 categories
• Full instant replay options
• Create-a-player, Create-a-roster
• Custom playoffs
• Player trades
• Season-ending awards
NBA Action 98

Suit up for another season of 100% pure NBA action. Real pro teams, pro players, pro plays, pro stats, pro everything! Motion capture technology, full commentary and up to 10 players at once makes this the most complete basketball game yet!
NBA Jam Extreme

Play two-on-two basketball using NBA teams that consist of six players each. The game play is three-dimensional instead of using the common 2D format. Game commentary is provided by Marv Albert.

Due to contractual obligations from acting in the 1996 movie Space Jam, a few players were not allowed to be featured in NBA Jam Extreme. Chief among those barred from appearing in NBA Jam Extreme were Michael Jordan and Charles Barkley. Shaquille O'Neal was unable to be featured in the game because of his contractual obligations to the movies Kazaam, Good Burger and the video game Shaq-Fu.
NBA Jam Tournament Edition

NBA Jam Tournament Edition is the second game in Midway’s basketball arcade series, featuring two-on-two fast paced matches with NBA players from the 1993-94 season (1994-95 on consoles). In total, the game features over 120 NBA athletes and over 40 hidden characters. Improvements include additional power-ups, more detailed player attributes, player substitutions after each quarter, and a new soundtrack. The namesake "Tournament Mode" turns off all cheats and power-ups, and rewards players with expanded rosters for nearly all teams if the player beats all 27 teams.
NBA Live 97

NBA Live 97 is a basketball game with an emphasis on realism. You can choose from all of the NBA teams, create a team with players you create yourself, or choose a team formed by the All-Star players of the east or West coasts. When you create a player yourself you can customize the player to a high degree. There are over 60 offensive and 10 defensive set-ups. Match options include an exhibition match, a whole season or the playoffs.
NBA Live 98

NBA Live 98 offers the player all teams, players and stadiums of the 1998 NBA season. More than 350 faces got scanned to improve realism. Also some new moves like crossover or fade-aways are implemented. You can play single games, whole seasons, the playoffs or new things like manager career or 3-point-shootout in the style of an all-star-game.
Nekketsu Oyako

Middle-aged housewife Saeko Hibino has a secret: she's actually a Nobel laureate theoretical physicist who devised a completely new type of antimatter fusion reactor at only 17 years old. But when a band of no-good bad guys calling themselves the Haraguro-dan find out, they figure she's perfect to help them complete their ultimate secret doomsday weapon and kidnap her. Her family aren't going to take this lying down, though, and immediately take up arms, setting out to free her by whatever means necessary!

Nekketsu Oyako ("Hot-Blooded Family") is a side-scrolling beat-'em-up in the tradition of Final Fight with a particular focus on finding and picking up weapons in each stage. There are three characters to choose from: Saeko's husband, former pro-wrestler Rando, their fighting prodigy daughter Rio, and Saeko's freeloading research assistant, Torataro Minowa. Each character has their own stats and special abilities, and two players can also play simultaneously.
Next King: Koi no Sennen Oukoku

In a country named Herb Land, several princes are preparing to the great competition, in the end of which one of them will become a king! But you, the young hero of the game (who also happens to be a prince), should know one important thing: if a prince doesn't have success with girls, he won't win the competition! And so, your quest for the crown and for the attention of the fairer sex begins...

Next King: Koi no Sennen Ōkoku is a mixture of a board game, dating simulation, and role-playing. It can also be described as a table RPG. You compete against three other princes, and must have more success with the game's several main female characters in order to become a king. Your actions in the game are determined by the roll of dice. It will tell you at what time of the week you'll be able to begin your turn, how many steps you take on the world map, how much damage you do in battles, and so on. When you visit a town, you should go to see the girls and take quests from them.
NFL '97

This version of the SEGA Sports NFL franchise was released only for the SEGA Saturn. It features all fully licensed NFL teams and their respective logos along with updated rosters for the 1996 NFL season. It also has the option to create a brand new NFL team from scratch if the player chooses to and even create their own plays that can be used in games.

The standard game modes apply here such as Exhibition, Season, etc. and keep extensive track of stats in over 70 different categories and over 150 offensive and defensive plays to choose from. Eight friends can also go against each other using multi-tap.
NFL Quarterback Club 96

Another game in NFL Quarterback series. Every team from the 1996 NFL season is shown here, with real player numbers and stats. 32 offensive plays and 16 defensive plays are available as you play. Options include setting quarter lengths, from one to 15 minutes, and selecting your mode of play: Preseason, Playoffs, or a full Season, in which you play 18 games towards the goal of the Super Bowl.
NFL Quarterback Club 97

NFL Quarterback Club 97 utilizes many of the same gameplay elements seen in Madden NFL 97 - including the kicking T-meter, the three-quarter overhead primary camera angle, and the button assignments and controls. Player animations are fluid and realistic, and the player sprites have clearly visible jersey numbers and names.

The game also boasts a historic simulation mode. Players can choose among 50 different classic NFL game situations and try to rewrite history. Imagine...it's December 23, 1973. The Dallas Cowboys are down 28-13 to the 49ers. With under a minute remaining, the Boys score a touchdown and recover an onside kick. Can you complete one of the greatest comebacks in NFL history?
NHL 97

1997 edition of EA's NHL sport simulation series. Improvements in this edition come mostly in the graphical arena, with a refined version of the "virtual stadium" system that adds new camera angles (including the classical top-down one strangely missing from NHL 96), and polygonal players instead of the bitmap-based ones with motion-captured animations.

Other extras include multiplayer support for up to 8 players through network or Gravis's GrIP system, the option to create new players and trade them around, and the usual amount of EA sports licensed multimedia flair, including an interesting "Goalie Mask Viewer" which lets you observe the elaboratedly decorated helmets of 30 goalies.
NHL 98

NHL 98 features much faster and refined gameplay (now using four action keys instead of two, removing the need to double-tap to perform some actions), along other new features such as "in-the-fly" tactics developed by Marc Crawford, then manager of the Colorado Avalanche and new commentary lines from Jim Hughson and Darryl Reaugh and a re-worked interface. Graphics are improved from the previous version with the players being less angular, and thanks to 3Dfx support, with less pixels showing in the textures. The in-game presentation follows a TV-style script, zooming in players while displaying stats during clock stoppages.

As far as game modes go, in the year of the first Olympic Tournament with professional players, NHL 98 introduced the first real international competition, with 18 International teams to choose from. Other game modes include Season (option to pick between 25 or 82 games) and Playoff (best of 1, 3, 5 or 7 matches) and a Penalty Shootout mode.
NHL All-Star Hockey

NHL All-Star Hockey is the first of Sega's own line of Saturn NHL licensed titles. It includes the ability to play pre-season matches, a full season or just the playoffs, as well as multimedia content, such as a tour of the NHL Hall of Fame in Toronto, information on the trophies and real player trading cards (from the Fleer Ultra collection). It's also possible to trade players and create players and teams for use in pre-season matches.

If a player owns two of Sega's 6 player adapters, all players can be controlled by human players, but in lesser number of human players, it's still possible to . Due to the large size of the league save games, the use of the external memory cartridge is advised.
NHL All-Star Hockey 98

NHL All-Star Hockey 98 is a hockey game where the player can control a team of his choice to bring it to victory and glory. The game modes are the typical genre choices: Either a whole NHL season, the NHL playoffs or a league with 15 national teams. The team logos and player names are official licensed and uses the data from 1996/1997.

The gameplay itself is more action oriented than a simulation and uses several shooting and pass variations which are activated with more or less complicated key combinations. Six camera angles and a instant replay feature complement the TV atmosphere.

The game also features several tactical possibilities. For eight game situations the player can choose between three behaviors, e.g. how the players set up shots in the offensive zone. During the season there is a option to trade players with other teams. Extensive mid-season statistics, which can be shown for every team in the league, help planning transfers and tactics.
NHL Powerplay '96

An early competitor to the EA Sports NHL series, NHL Powerplay '96 features motion-captured players, an NHL Player’s Association license, a variety of managerial options, and the ability to play seasons and tournaments.

It is the first NHL game to include a World Tournament mode in which the NHL players can compete against each other on their respective national teams.

In a time where developers tried to get the most from 32-bit consoles, leading to the "unlimited camera angles" blurb on many games, NHL Powerplay stuck with the one most people used, the overhead "behind the goal" view, popularized by EA's NHL series - and it was one of first full 3D sports games on the market.
Night Striker S

Night Striker is a third-person shooter reminiscent of Space Harrier. Laser optics expert Dr. Lindvery Maska and his daughter have been kidnapped by a terrorist group, and Dick Dagras, head of the Special Service Agency, is mobilizing a group of elite soldiers experienced in the use of special armored flying cars, in order to rescue Dr. Maska and destroy this terrorist group.

The player flies through each stage, controlling their armored car and shooting down waves of enemies. A boss appears at the end of each stage, and after this the player must choose what path to take in the next stage, as in Darius. Instead of lives, the player has a shield that takes damage from each hit, but is recharged at the end of each stage.

The Saturn version features a set of exclusive bonus levels.
Night Warriors: Darkstalkers' Revenge

The Darkstalkers return and now crave the fury of a good night fight. In this head-to-head fighting challenge, creatures from your darkest nightmares battle for eternal control fo the night. Treacherous, classic favorites take on 4 new challengers for total domination. Donovan, the Dark Hunter. Huitzil, the Killer Machine. Hsien-Ko, the Chinese Ghost. And Pyron, the ultimate Alien ruler. The battle has never been as intense, with faster speeds, more captivating moves and even more incredible graphics. Night Warriors; the game of your dreams, and nightmares.
Nightruth: Explanation of the Paranormal #01 - "Yami no Tobira"

Shinya Izayoi is not your average high-school student. He's knowledgeable in black magic, wears a ring that summons a magical sword, and is part of a group of students that investigates paranormal activity. Strange events such as spontaneous combustion have been happening recently, so Shinya and his (mostly cute and female) friends are drawn in to get to the truth of what's happening.

Nightruth is a visual novel-style adventure game following the adventures of a team of high school students who use their supernatural abilities to to investigate paranormal events. The game plays out as standard for this type of game, consisting of voiced and illustrated story scenes with occasional player choices; these choices branch off via player choice into one of three different storylines, each of which has multiple possible endings.

A music CD containing the game's theme song is also included in the package.
Nightruth: Explanation of the Paranormal: "Futatsu Dake no Shinjitsu"

"Futatsu Dake no Shinjitsu" ("The Only Two Truths") is the third and final game in the Nightruth series, this time starring the youngest of Shinya's classmates, Ai Himekawa. The story focuses on her previously unexplained powers of precognition and telekinesis. Gameplay is again similar to the visual novel-style adventure presentation of the previous entries, featuring voiced and illustrated story sequences which occasionally branch via player choice into multiple endings. However, rather than featuring stories about famous supernatural phenomena, the focus this time is strictly on the main characters and their own personal stories.
Nightruth: Explanation of the Paranormal: "Maria"

Maria is the second game in the Nightruth series, following up after Yami no Tobira and this time focusing on one of the female leads, Maria Mizunagi, a fellow student of Shinya's who is skilled at fighting and possesses a supernatural healing ability.

Gameplay is identical to the visual novel-style adventure presentation of the previous title — voiced and illustrated story sequences which occasionally branch via player choice into multiple scenarios, each with multiple endings. This entry features stories relating to three famous historical events: Jack the Ripper, the Mary Celeste, and the Miracle of the Sun.
Nightruth: Explanation of the Paranormal: Making of Nightruth II: Voice Selection
Nightruth: Explanation of the Paranormal: Making of Nightruth II: Voice Selection is a multimedia disc for the Sega Saturn. It contains a trailer to Nightruth#01 and #02.
Nightruth: Explanation of the Paranormal: Nightruth Voice Selection: Radio Drama-hen
Nightruth Voice Selection: Radio Drama Hen (ナイトゥルース ヴォイスセレクション ラジオドラマ編) is a multimedia disc for the Sega Saturn. It contains a making movie of voice drama, and trailer to Nightruth#03.
Nightruth: Explanation of the Paranormal: The Making of Nightruth
The Making of Nightruth (ザ・メイキング・オブ・ナイトゥルース) is a multimedia disc for the Sega Saturn. It is the FanDisc of Nightruth: Yami no Tobira.
NiGHTS into Dreams...

Immerse yourself in an unparalleled 3D flying experience. NiGHTS truly delivers an amazing virtual world of dreams - filled with unbelievable real-time effects, fantastic creatures and nightmarish monsters.

• A masterful showcase of Sega Saturn's raging processing power.
• Face your worst nightmares in a stunning world of 3D gameplay.
• Dozens of camera angles, never-seen-before effects and 3D positional sound.
• Developed exclusively for Sega Saturn by the creators of "Sonic the Hedgehog."
NiGHTS into Dreams: Pedestrian Challenge

If you’re playing NiGHTS Into Dreams correctly, you won’t do much walking around as Elliot or Claris: it’s a short distance from the beginning of each stage to the Ideya Palace where NiGHTS is, and if you don’t run out the clock, you’ll be flying the rest of the time.

Pre-release coverage of NiGHTS suggest that the Elliot / Claris gameplay might have been more substantial during development — some videos show the Ideya Palaces in other locations, so maybe you had to hunt for them?

What would NiGHTS be like with more platforming? Saturn ROM hacker bbayles decided to make the dream real. Introducing NiGHTS Into Dreams: Pedestrian Challenge, a mod that makes NiGHTS into a 3D platformer.

In Pedestrian Challenge, you need all five Ideya to free NiGHTS from the Ideya Palace. At the start of each Dream, approach the Ideya Palace to stash the red Ideya. You’ll be knocked back from the Ideya Palace once you touch it.
Nihon Daihyou Team no Kantoku ni Naruu! Sekaihatsu Soccer RPG

In this game you are the Japanese national soccer team coach, who manages, trains, trades, and does whatever a coach does and much more. You also develop team strategy and travel to other countries to discover hidden great players. For each stadium game, it features TV coverage and your team technical progress.
Nihon Pro Mahjong Renmei Kounin: Doujou Yaburi
Nihon Pro Mahjong Renmei Kounin Doujou Yaburi (日本プロ麻雀連盟公認 道場破り) is a mahjong game for the Sega Saturn.
Nile-gawa no Yoake

Nile-gawa no Yoake ("Dawn on the Nile River") is a city-building simulation game with war strategy elements in which the player takes the role of a Pharaoh in ancient Egypt. Starting in the capital of Memphis, the player must build the city up not just in its buildings and infrastructure, but also in its culture and military might. Population, taxes, and cultural development all determine what structures and actions are allowed, and buildings will also decay over time and must be repaired.

War can be waged with neighboring regions, and defeating them will add their territory to your own. Battles take place in real-time with the player directly issuing commands to their army. The ultimate goal of the game is to unify the entirety of the Mediterranean under your Pharaoh's rule. If the Pharaoh dies, their successor will continue their rule, though this can only happen a certain number of times before the game is over.
Ninja Jajamaru-kun: Onigiri Ninpouchou Gold

Ninja Jajamaru-kun: Onigiri Ninpouchou Gold is a 3D platformer in the Ninja Jajamaru-kun series. It has gameplay similar to that of Ninja Jajamaru-kun: Onigiri Ninpouchou, in which players control the ninja protagonist Jajamaru-kun from a fixed behind-view perspective while using his throwable shuriken and katana to dispatch enemies, but with entirely different levels and enemies. The story once again follows Jajamaru-kun on a quest to rescue Princess Sakura from the clutches of Catfish Tayu. Like the previous game, levels contain power-ups for Jajamaru-kun to collect, and defeating enemies and collecting silver pieces awards points which add up to a score at the end of each level.

Although most of the game takes place in 3D environments, it also includes some 2D levels in the style of the original Ninja Jajamaru-kun game so that the 2D and 3D approaches to the series can be directly compared.
Ninku: Tsuyoki na Yatsura no Daigekitotsu!

Ninku: Tsuyoki na Yatsura no Daigekitotsu! is a one-on-one fighting game based on the manga and anime series Ninku. It features cel-animated characters on 3D backgrounds and includes eight playable characters from the series. The game is a versus fighter in the vein of Street Fighter II, and each character has a variety of unique moves, as well as special moves that can only be executed when their special power bar has enough charge. There is a single-player arcade mode and a two-player versus mode.
Ninpen Manmaru

Ninpen Manmaru is a 3D action platform game based on the anime and manga known internationally as Manmaru the Ninja Penguin. The story is simple: Manmaru has been sent by his master to train on his own and hone his ninja skills, and his rivals show up to try and thwart him. The game is broken into six themed stages, which each consists of four areas and a boss fight. Each area is a relatively compact area, and the objective is simply to find and reach the goal while collecting coins and avoiding enemies. Boss fights do not involve direct combat, but are instead various competitive minigames, such as a race to collect more coins than the opponent or to be the first to find the exit to a maze.
Nissan Presents: Over Drivin' GT-R

Over Drivin' GT-R is a heavily localised version of Road & Track Presents The Need for Speed, with all the cars replaced by vehicles produced by Nissan Motor Company (plus a few with Datsun branding). Japanese Saturn owners never received The Need for Speed itself, though PlayStation owners did in the form of Over Drivin' DX (to distinguish from the original 3DO version).

Though much of the core engine remains the same as The Need for Speed, many of the tracks in Over Drivin' GT-R are unlocked from the start, there are minor sound changes and FMV and graphics replacements. Whereas the original version features a number of similar cars that can compete with each other, this version of the game is simply meant to illustrate a history of varying Nissan vehicles. Gameplay is also slower than The Need for Speed.
No-appointment Gals Olympos

A high-school student named Noboru has a curious ability: when he dreams, he appears in a strange realm that seems almost to be as real as the waking world. Usually these travels vanish from his thoughts like any other dream, but one night he meets a mysterious woman who seems to recognize him and tells him he must leave and never return. Thinking she looks familiar, he chases after her in hopes of learning more, but winds up waking up before he finds her. Together with his fairy companion Nirvana, Noboru decides to search for this woman and learn more about the strange realm he continues to find himself in.

No-appointment Gals Olympos is a fantasy adventure game in which the player summons girls to fight on their behalf. The game is divided into two major parts.
Nobunaga no Yabou Returns

Nobunaga no Yabou Returns is a remake of the original Nobunaga's Ambition from 1983. The strategy gameplay is identical to the original release — select either Oda Nobunaga or Takeda Shingen and attempt to conquer the 17 regions of Kansai and central Japan — but this remake features completely redone graphics and sound. All daimyo are now rendered in full 3D, and there is a full remixed soundtrack including many songs appearing from other Nobunaga's Ambition games.
Nobunaga no Yabou Sengoku Gunyuuden

Nobunaga's Ambition II is the sequel to Nobunaga's Ambition. The setting is 16th century feudal Japan, a period when ruthless daimyo (feudal lords) contended with each other for dominance. Ultimately, the winner in this struggle will become Shogun and hold actual power over the islands, while being nominally subject to the Emperor.

The game casts the player as one of the daimyo, allowing them freedom to decide the fate and future of feudal Japan, through diplomacy and ultimately war. The objective is to unify Japan under the player's rule. If the player fails through death on the battlefield, assassination at the hands of a ninja, or through natural causes, they can choose a successor and play on. Functionally, the first job is to let prosper the fief (province) under the player's control through agricultural development and town investment.
Nobunaga no Yabou: Shouseiroku
Nobunaga no Yabou: Shouseiroku is a turn-based tactical strategy game set in 16th century feudal Japan. It is the seventh title in the Nobunaga's Ambition series.
Nobunaga no Yabou: Tenshouki

Nobunaga no Yabou: Tenshouki is a tactical strategy game set in 16th century feudal Japan. It is the sixth game in the Nobunaga's Ambition war simulation series. The player can educate warlords and increase their fighting power. He/she can let them go into battle and check their statuses in the meantime. It is possible to have dozens of opponents fighting alone in a given scenario.
Nobunaga no Yabou: Tenshouki with Power-Up Kit

Nobunaga no Yabou: Tenshouki with Power-Up Kit is a re-released version of the same game for the Sega Saturn, adding the contents of the game's expansion pack (or "power-up kit" as it is known in this context).
Nonomura Byouin no Hitobito

The principal of Nonomura hospital has killed himself. Or so it appears at first sight. But the private detective Takumaro Kaibara is not so sure about that. Maybe it was a suicide, but maybe it was a murder. To find out what has really happened, Kaibara heads to Nonomura hospital. It should be mentioned that Kaibara is famous not only for his talent as a detective, but also for his skills as a seducer. And it is also known that Nonomura hospital is full of beautiful nurses. To kill two birds with one stone, Kaibara tries to make his way to the hearts of the sexy nurses, at the same time gathering information for the crime investigation. Will he be able to succeed in both?

Nonomura Byōin no Hitobito contains erotic images and scenes and is marked for the ages 18+.
Noon

Noon is a multiplayer puzzle game that allows up to four players. It takes the overhead gameplay style of Bomberman and mixes it with standard puzzle style gameplay. Your goal is to cover your opponents playfield with bombs. 

Bombs are made by connecting a row of three or more balls and attacking them, causing them to “explode” and reappear as bombs on your opponents playfield. This is called a NOON. There are five different colors: Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue and Multi/Rainbow. When lining up the balls, they must all be the same color. The lone exception being the multi color, or rainbow balls which you can mix with any one of the other colors. Rainbow balls are key to Rainbow NOONs. These are like regular NOONs only when the Rainbow Ball or balls explode it will make adjacent balls explode as well, regardless of color. 

Once you fill your opponents playfield with bombs a counter will begin to countdown from 10. Upon zero you will be victorious.
Norse by Norsewest: The Return of the Lost Vikings

Their lost is your game.

The lost boys are back: Erik the Swift; Baleog the Fierce and Olaf the Stout. This action-strategy game is not for the lame of brain. In their adventure, the trio escaped from the evil alien captor Tomator. Now, armed with all new high-tech weaponry the boys heisted from Tomator, they set out to find the time machine that will land them back home. It’s your challenge to complete each of the levels with all three Vikings alive and kickin’!

• Totally new characters – Scorch the fire-breathing dragon and Fang the werewolf
• Fly, shrink, hover and more with 5 hilarious characters, each equipped with unique abilities
• 31 level of mind-bending play
• 5 different worlds with endless terrain and a host of fierce enemies
• Beautifully rendered 3D characters and environments
• 1 or 2 players
Noël 3: Not Digital

Save the students snatched away by terrorists in adventure game Noël 3: Not Digital. In addition to mystery-solving elements, a thrilling storyline and wealth of animation deliver an enhanced gameplay.
O-chan no Oekaki Logic

Oh-chan no Oekaki Logic is a digital conversion, with anime mascots, of the classic Japanese newspaper puzzle nonograms. A nonogram is a puzzle on a square or rectangular grid the object of which is to reveal a hidden picture. Along each row and column there is a number or series of numbers which indicate how many squares will be colored in that row or grid. Example; "5 9 4" would mean there would be sets of five, nine, and four colored squares in the grid, in that order, with at least one blank in between. 

Oh-chan no Oekaki Logic adds a story mode where starring the titular character, Hebereke's friend who first appeared in Ufouria: The Saga. Oh-Chan, representing the player, competes with other blobby anime characters in finding hidden images in the nonogram grids.
Ochige Designer: Tsukutte Pon!

Ochige Designer: Tsukutte Pon! is a game creation tool that lets the player make their own customized falling-block puzzle game. It is possible to customize the game rules, including how pieces are cleared, as well as the well size and orientation, piece and character graphics, and even the title screen. Various rule sets are available, in the style of games including Tetris, Columns, Puyo Puyo, and Panic Bomber. There are six different sample games included in the package, which demonstrate the tool's various features and configuration options.
Off-World Interceptor Extreme

You play a Trashman, a bounty hunter paid to capture criminal scum hiding on harsh alien worlds.

Your job is to race the enemy crime boss to the finish, blasting his goons along the way. Get blown up or drive too slowly and the boss gets away. But if you make it to the check point in time, you block the boss' escape and trap him on the planet.

You can upgrade your vehicle with the cash from your bounties. You can also go up against a buddy in the vertical split-screen deathmatch mode.

Off-World Interceptor's most unique feature is the storyline, told in full-motion video. Standard for the time. But OWIE's FMV is mocked by a couple of guys sitting in chairs, a la Mystery Science Theater 3000.
Ojousama Express

Ojousama Express is a love adventure game set on a cross-country luxury train traveling across Japan. The journey takes a total of 15 days, with the train stopping at various cities and tourist destinations throughout the country. The protagonist is taking the trip hoping to meet girls, and many lovely ladies will get on or off the train at different stops along the trip.

The game is generally divided into sections where the train is running, and sections where it is stopped at a destination. While the train is running, the player can move between the cars, looking for girls to talk to; characters have no fixed schedules, but rather will move on their own based on their preferences and current relationships. In addition to the passenger cars, there is also a shop to buy guides for the next stop, a restaurant to meet up with the girls, the conductor's car where hints can be had, and an entertainment car with a selection of minigames.
Ojousama o Nerae!!

Ojousama o Nerae!! is a visual novel-style love adventure game. The protagonist, Kenji Yamamura, is a high school senior who should be studying for his college entrance exams, but has instead decided to confess his love to the girl he's infatuated with — Mitsuki Saitōin — in hopes of spending the summer with her instead. But she seems completely out of his league, and so it won't be as simple as just writing her a single letter.

The game progresses in basic visual-novel style, with the player selecting dialogue options at certain points during conversations and occasionally selecting which location to go to next from a list. There are a total of 7 different possible romantic interests to pursue, including Mitsuki herself. The original PC version of the game includes explicit sexual content, which is censored to only the minimum degree necessary for the Sega Saturn release.
Okudera Yasuhiko no Sekai o Mezase! Soccer Kids: Nyuumon-hen

Okudera Yasuhiko no Sekai wo Mezase! Soccer Kids: Nyuumon Hen (奥寺康彦の世界を目指せ！ サッカーキッズ 入門編) is an educational game developed by JAMP and published by Fujitsu Parex for the Sega Saturn. It it is aimed at teaching children about football (soccer), and features former Japanese footballer Yasuhiko Okudera, who was manager of JEF United Ichihara Chiba when the game was released.
Olympic Soccer

While the soccer tournament is often downplayed not only inside the Olympic movement, but also by the soccer-following community, in 1996, by the occasion of the Games of the XXVI Olympiad in Atlanta, US Gold decided to release a game representing the tournament.

The player can choose one of the 33 teams, and participate on exhibition matches, arcade (a 32-team cup knockout), Olympic (the 16 team tournament mimicking the actual tournament) or play on an all-versus-all league (from 3 to 16 teams). The games features the usual options found in contemporary games, such as match length and draw rules, as well as define several weather patterns from wind to the bumpiness of the grass. All 5 stadiums used in the actual Olympics are present.
Omakase! Savers

Hinako, Kana, and Wakaba are three high school girls and the best of friends. One day they're goofing around at a shrine taking photos, and accidentally break a seal and release 108 spirits that had been sealed there. These spirits are terribly mischievous, and even turn one of the girls' classmates -- who was with them taking the photos -- into a strange mystical gem! The old man who watches over the shrine confronts the girls, telling them that it's their fault that the spirits escaped. They are each granted a secret transformation power that allows them to fight the sprits, and now it's their responsibility to capture the spirits and seal them back up again.

Omakase! Savers is a comedy adventure game featuring live-action scenes. The player takes the role of the girls' classmate, who appears as a small ghost, and must guide the girls in their quest to seal the spirits again and restore their classmate to his human form.
Ooedo Renaissance

Ooedo Renaissance is an economic simulation game based on an earlier PC release. This conversion of the game retains the same general premise and structure, but makes several major changes; most notably, the game has changed from a real-time progression to turn-based, with the player deciding all their actions and policy changes on a month-by-month basis. This version also completely overhauls the visual style, with an isometric perspective of the city and a new cartoonish look to the characters. It also puts more emphasis on story elements and specific objectives to provide more guidance to the player over the sandbox experience of the original game.
Ousama Game

In Ousama Game the player challenges various young women to simple games, and if the girl loses they must do whatever the player asks. There are three different mini-games, selected at random by a roulette: a rock-paper-scissors-style game where the losing player must react quickly to block an attack; a flags-style game where the player must push buttons according to an announcer's instructions; and a simple action game where the player must climb a bamboo shoot while avoiding falling objects. Upon winning a game, the player can select from a list of actions they can force the girl to do, such as "go for a swim" or "take a shower", and watch a video clip of them doing as ordered. There are eight girls to challenge, each of whom has numerous different situations and video clips to see.
P.T.O.: Pacific Theater of Operations II

Target or be targeted!

1941 and the Two opponents. Two strategies. The year is scene is the Pacific. Japanese Zeros appear on the horizon, marking the beginning of World War II. From Pearl Harbor to unconditional surrender, this is your battlefield. PTO II delivers the power to control this infamous war. With new technology, faster and better war machines are at your disposal.

Command the guns of the mighty Missouri, launch devastating Japanese fighter attacks, or storm the beaches of Okinawa. India, Australia, and the east coast of the United States mark new regions for enemy domination.
Pachi-Slot Kanzen Kouryaku Uni-Colle '97: Universal Collection

Pachi-Slot Kanzen Kouryaku Uni-Colle '97: Universal Collection is a pachi-slot (Japanese slot machine) simulation game featuring digital recreations of eight real-life pachi-slot machines made by Universal and its subsidiaries: Baby Angel 2, Getter Mouse, Frozen Nights, Taco Slot, CC Angel, Dunk Shoot 2, Super Mog Mog 2, and Cranky Condor. Each machine is faithfully recreated, and the player can choose from six different manufacturer's settings to practice various configurations. The game includes detailed stat tracking for each machine.
Pachinko Hall: Shinsou Daikaiten

Pachinko Hall: Shinsou Daikaiten is a business simulation game where the player runs a chain of pachinko parlors. The protagonist takes over the business from their father after his retirement, and starting from a single location, the goal is to grow the business enough within 20 years to take the company public and list it on the stock exchange. Using a menu-based system, the game includes detailed simulation of all aspects of operating a pachinko hall franchise, from obvious elements such as hiring employees and determining prizes and payouts, to more esoteric elements such as negotiating loans and obtaining the proper government permits to open new locations.
Pad Nifty

Pad Nifty (パッドニフティ) is a piece of Sega Saturn software released exclusively in Japan. It was used to access Fujitsu's now defunct NIFTY-Serve network. Sega had a presence on NIFTY-Serve with their Sega Game Information Station, with the network having previously hosted dedicated Sega bulletin boards.

It is completely reliant on the Sega Saturn Modem (of which it was bundled with) and the defunct NIFTY-Serve network, as such it cannot function in the modern age.
Pad Nifty 1.1 & Habitat II

This bundle includes three pieces of software for exclusive use with the Sega Saturn Modem, collected onto one disc:

• Habitat II (online virtual world game, previously only sold bundled with a keyboard accessory)
• Pad Nifty 1.1 (message board browser software, previously only sold bundled with the Modem accessory)
• An internet browser application
Pandemonium!

The young sorceress Nikki, the court jester Fargus, and his side-kick Sid the puppet are the three main protagonists of this 3D platform game. While attending a "Wizards in Training" seminar, Nikki accidentally casts a powerful magic spell, which results in a giant monsters swallowing the whole village. The three friends must now travel to a place called "Wishing Engine", and be granted a wish to revert the world back to normal.

The characters each have a special movement to kill enemies with. The game uses floating camera angles through a vast Prince of Persia-style world. The goal of the game is to clear the various levels, avoiding spikes and enemies and collecting coins for extra lives.

Unlike most 3D platformers, Pandemonium offers only two-dimensional movement, rather than complete freedom of movement. The characters move along a curving 2D course within a 3D environment.
Paneltia Story: Kerun no Daibouken

A boy named Kerun lives a rather boring life. One night, he spots a shooting star in the sky and makes a wish, but winds up getting more than he bargained for! The star hears him and appears before him to grant his wish, and he's whisked away through a portal to the land of Paneltia, where he must take up a sword and become the hero of this fantastic realm.

Paneltia Story is a Japanese-style RPG with a twist: the world the player explores isn't fixed, but rather is constructed by the player as it is being explored. The player collects various "panels" representing different locations and types of terrain from enemies, item boxes, and shops; these can be placed on the map to create new areas to explore and find yet more panels. The game is divided up into stages, with the goal of each stage generally being to build up enough experience and strength to defeat a boss hidden somewhere in the map.
Panic-chan

Kengo is an average guy working at a video rental store. One day, his boss asks him to make an ad for recruiting female employees for the store, hoping that a cute face at the counter might help business. While Kengo is working on the ad on his computer, a cute girl suddenly appears on the screen; this rather flustered and excitable young lady introduces herself as Panic, and before long she appears in the real world and starts working at the video store. However, while she might attract customers, she also attracts trouble, and soon another mysterious lady starts appearing on video screens. Just who are these two girls, and what is their connection?

Panic-chan is a visual-novel style adventure game with a focus on animated sequences; it describes itself as an "OVA adventure" and includes 90 minutes of original animation.
Panzer Dragoon

Thousands of years have passed since the Ancient Age; humanity struggles for survival in an unforgiving world. The player takes control of Kyle Fluge, a hunter caught up in a struggle between two dragons, and given an enormous task. Armed with an ancient gun and riding atop the Blue Dragon, you must battle against mutated wildlife, the covetous empire, and ancient sentinels, all for the sake of fulfilling the task entrusted to you by the Blue Dragon's prior rider - do not let the Black Dragon reach the Tower.
Panzer Dragoon II: Zwei

Flash backwards to several years before the vicious battle against the Black Dragon in the original Panzer Dragoon. In a small village in the country of Meccania, coolias are bred for use as beasts of burden. Mutant coolias with glowing throats are killed, for they are bad omens, but one villager, Jean-Jacques Lundi, is unable to bring himself to kill his coolia Lagi - for Lagi has wings!
When an ancient ship arrives and destroys the village a year later, Lagi exhibits the ability to fire lasers from his mouth! Lundi and Lagi set out in pursuit of the ancient ship - for revenge, or perhaps for other reasons...
Panzer Dragoon Playable Preview

Panzer Dragoon Playable Preview (unnamed in Europe) is a demo disc containing a shortened version of Panzer Dragoon for the Sega Saturn. Only episode 2 is playable, and is assumed to be identical to the full product.

This disc was bundled with Saturn consoles for a short period in both North America and Europe. It was not released elsewhere, nor did it see a separate commercial release.
Panzer Dragoon Saga

Enter the world of Panzer Dragoon Saga and experience a game like no other: a fusion of classic Panzer action with the most technologically advanced RPG to come to Saturn. Board your morphing dragon and behold as the mysteries of the Panzer world unfurl across four massive CDs. The new "rail free" 3D engine lets you soar deeper into role-playing adventure than you ever before imagined. Your destiny awaits.
Pappara Paoon

Pappara Paoon is a competitive color-matching puzzle game. Two players at opposite ends of a playfield launch colored pieces at a group of blocks; if four or more pieces of the same color are matched, all connected pieces of the same color are removed from play. Certain pieces will place garbage pieces on the opposing player's side of the board or shift the entire playfield in one direction, and if the pieces reach all the way to one end of the playfield, that player loses. The game includes both a single-player campaign mode and a two-player versus mode.
Parodius
This compilation collects the first two arcade incarnations of Konami's shoot'em'up parody series on one disc: Parodius: Non-sense Story and Fantastic Journey.
Pastel Muses

Pastel Muses is a puzzle game where you shoot colored balls down a slope to match them up with the pile of balls at the bottom. The premise is similar to such games as Puzzle Bobble, but with a difference. Here you not only control the aim, but also how hard you shoot the ball, making it go in an arc across the playing field and down the slope. Also, when you make balls disappear the remaining balls fall further down the slope using somewhat good physics.

You can play the game in the usual Story Mode, vs Mode and Endless Mode varieties usually found in this kind of puzzler.
PD Ultraman Link

PD Ultraman Link is a falling-block puzzle game featuring the Japanese superhero Ultraman and many of his allies and foes. Blocks of various colors fall into the well in pairs; each block has two connections, and connecting three or more blocks together regardless of color will cause them to disappear. Any blocks above the ones removed will fall into the now-open space, potentially creating chain combos which will send garbage blocks that must be cleared twice to the opponent. Additionally, connecting four blocks of the same color will clear all blocks of that color from the board, while connecting four each of a different color together will clear all the garbage blocks on the screen by one stage. If the blocks stack past the line at the top of the well, that player loses the match.

The game includes a single-player story mode, as well as a free battle mode against the computer or another player. There are 10 different characters to choose from: five Ultra Heroes and five aliens.
Pebble Beach Golf Links

Up to six players can play a round of golf on the world-famous Pebble Beach golf course in Sega Sports' Pebble Beach Golf Links. It features seven play modes including Tournament, Stroke Play, Skins Play, and Match Play, and narration and strategy by golf pro Craig Stadler. You also have the option of creating your own player and selecting your own custom set of golf clubs to challenge Craig Stadler and other AI players on the course. Stats, such as handicaps and course records, are tracked throughout the game. Also, if you ever tire of taking on your friends and the AI, you can play the game in Watch Mode and simply lay back and watch Craig Stadler take on the competition on the Pebble Beach course.
PGA Tour 97

Players can choose to play as one of fourteen professional golfers such as Fuzzy Zoeller and Jim Gallagher Jr. or choose to create their own golfer by giving them a name and choosing what their golfer looks like from the few portraits that are available.

Players are then able to select what type of game mode they want to play. Game modes include letting the player practice a round of golf, compete in a tournament, have a shoot-out, or compete in a Skins game.

The game features two 18 hole golf courses to play at. Both platform versions of this game include the Sawgrass golf course, with each also including a unique golf course of their own. The Playstation version includes the Spanish Bay links, while the Saturn version includes the Spyglass Hill course.

When on the course, player select what club they want to use. They also can set the angle, pitch and backspin of the ball before taking a swing. They then have to aim where they want their shot to go.
Phantasm

A writer named Adrienne Delaney has just moved into an old mansion with her photographer husband Donald. Shortly after moving in, Adrienne begins to experience horrifying nightmares and have odd encounters inside the creepy old abode. Furthermore, the house is having a severe effect on her husband, changing him for the worse. Adrienne must discover the secret of the house before the unknown force consumes her husband, and unravel the terrible events that have happened in the past.

Phantasmagoria is an adventure game that places heavy emphasis on full motion video for exposition and cutscenes at various junctures to advance the storyline. Adrienne is represented as a digitized character roaming around pre-rendered settings in the house. She inspects various rooms, finds items, adds them to her inventory, finds places to use the items, and triggers advancements in the plot.

Puzzle-solving element is present, though reduced compared to most other adventure games made by Sierra.
Photo Genic

Photo Genic is a love adventure game in which the player takes the part of a budding professional photographer. The protagonist is skilled at landscape photography, but has been tasked by his editor to prepare a gallery for an upcoming photo contest. The subject for this contest is photos of young girls, and so the protagonist must both find models and learn how to properly photograph them within the one-year deadline before the contest.

The player must determine their schedule for each week; as a professional photographer, the protagonist works five days a week and can use those days to train different aspects of their craft or to work various jobs in order to make money to buy supplies. On the weekend, the player is given one free day to visit locations around town, looking for models and eventually doing photo shoots. There are three different girls to approach, and the player's relationship with that girl will affect both their suitability and willingness as a model.
Pia Carrot e Youkoso!!

In Pia Carrot e Youkoso!! the player controls Yusuke Kinoshita, a 18-year-old male Japanese high-school student. He intends to have a cool summer vacation, but realizes he has no money. Having no choice, he takes a job in his father's restaurant, "Pia Carrot". Thus begins an adventure much more exciting than the summer vacation he has dreamed about: he gets to know many beautiful girls in the restaurant, and has to decide which one is the love of his life...

The game is a true dating simulation, with the gameplay focusing on making schedules and choosing activities for the protagonist. In the beginning of each day, the player typically choose an action before it's time to go to work. These actions range from giving a call to any of the girls the hero meets during the game, going to different locations, simply resting, etc. While at work, the player should make a schedule for Yusuke, sending him to work in different places (kitchen, basement, counter, etc.).
Pia Carrot e Youkoso!! 2

Pia Carrot e Youkoso!! 2 is a dating simulation game and a follow-up to the first game. Set four years later, the Pia Carrot restaurant has proved successful, and a second location has now opened. High school senior Kōji Maeda needs a part-time job over the simmer, and winds up working at the restaurant and living in its dormitory alongside numerous cute ladies.

Gameplay is quite similar to the previous title, with the player determining Kōji's schedule and actions for each day. Work days are decided each Thursday for the following week, and each day is divided into three sections. In the morning, Kōji can take various actions such as to study, exercise, or visit various locations around town. In the afternoon, he must go to work, and different tasks will improve different attributes. In the evening, he can approach one of the girls to strike up a conversation.
Pict Flash Dondon
Pict Flash Dondon (ピクトフラッシュどんどん) is an educational software for the Sega Saturn for children of ages 1 to 6 years old.
Pinball Graffiti

This pinball game has a 3D orientation in which the camera pans vertically wherever the ball moves or sometimes shows a closeup of the ball in rails and sinkholes. There are three different pinball tables:

• Basketball Legend - Has the theme of a basketball court with coach-styled messages.
• Card Master - Based on a casino theme, featuring poker and roulette.
• Circus Fantasia - Displays a circus-styled theme with scoring for stunts.

The two modes in the game are the pinball mode, which feature only the pinball tables for the highest score or the story mode. In the story mode, a crippled basketball college student goes to a bar where he is inspired to become the best pinball champion player in the United States. The career-styled gameplay requires the player to make use of limited funds to make purchases, travel between cities and resting to stay healthy. Money is earned by beating opponents' scores in pinball or by winning a basketball mini-game.
Planet Joker

Planet Joker is a vertically-scrolling shoot-em-up with a strong story presentation. A mysterious army has invaded Tokyo, and it's up to a special crack team of JSDF mech pilots to defeat the invaders. The player chooses from one of seven different mech suits, each of which has different stats and a different set of attack abilities. In addition to regular shots and bombs, there is also a charged shot, and three different weapon types which can be swapped and upgraded by collecting items throughout each of the seven stages. There are also two competition modes: a time-attack mode to reach a set score as quickly as possible, and a caravan-style score attack mode with a time limit.
Playboy Karaoke Collection Volume 1

Playboy Karaoke Collection Volume 1 (プレイボーイカラオケVol.1) is a 1996 compilation of karaoke music videos with Playboy models in the background released by VIC Tokai for the Sega Saturn exclusively in Japan. A second volume was also made.
Playboy Karaoke Collection Volume 2

Playboy Karaoke Collection Volume 2 (プレイボーイカラオケvol.2) is a 1996 compilation of karaoke music videos with Playboy models in the background released by VIC Tokai for the Sega Saturn exclusively in Japan. A first volume was also made.
Pocket Fighter

What happens when you take several signature Capcom fighters, squish them down into chibi (small or SD) versions of themselves, and give them a whole collection of wacky moves and over-the-top costumes? You get Pocket Fighter! Take on one of several pint-sized Capcom characters in this wacky, colorful fighting game.
Policenauts

In the year 2010 mankind has built its first space colony, Beyond Coast. Three years later the founders of the colony felt it needed to be protected, and chose five best policemen from Earth to do that: Gates Becker from Scotland Yard, the Japanese Sadaoki Tokugawa, Salvatore Toscanini from New York, and two policemen from Los Angeles: Jonathan Ingram and his best friend Ed Brown. During a routine patrol on Beyond Coast, something happened to Jonathan's space suit. He was sucked into space and presumed dead. Twenty-five years later, he is miraculously discovered in his life pod, alive. He still looks like a young man, but in reality he is fifty-five years old.

Trying to forget his past, Jonathan opens an investigation agency on Earth. One day, his ex-wife unexpectedly pays him a visit. She has re-married during Jonathan's prolonged absence, and asks him to find her missing husband. When she leaves the office, her car explodes, and she dies.
Powerslave

An ancient evil force, neither of this time nor of this world, has remained buried since the Egyptians walked the earth. Now it has been exhumed. Of course, you, the hero, must find out what's going on in Egypt. Your helicopter crashes within this danger zone and you must survive on your own. Meet the Egyptian gods and follow their advice.
